items.title: InnoCarnival 2026 exhibits I&T achievements to let dreams take flight (with photos)
items.description: Organised by the Innovation and Technology Commission, InnoCarnival 2026 (IC 2026) is being held for nine consecutive days from today (October 24) to November 1 at the Hong Kong Science Park in Sha Tin. Public admission is free. Under the theme "Lead with I&T Dream to Fly High", this year's carnival not only showcases a number of exhibits of local innovation and technology (I&T) achievements, but also features an aerospace thematic zone to showcase relevant research projects of local universities and their contributions to the country's space exploration missions. Speaking at the opening ceremony, the Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, said that Hong Kong's strong frontier research capabilities, comprehensive financial services and world-class international talent together provide a complete pathway for turning ideas into industries. Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, announced by the Government last month, positions the Northern Metropolis as a hub for I&T industries, promoting the integrated development of education, technology, talent and industry to closely align university talent development and research with industry needs. The Government will also leverage Hong Kong's financial strengths to channel more patient capital into supporting research teams and start-ups as they progress from research and development (R&D) to application. Mr Chan noted that I&T development ultimately depends on people, particularly the younger generation. Through exhibitions, workshops, talks and interactive experiences, IC 2026 enables members of the public to learn through hands-on participation. Citing the mobile food-waste paper machine that won the junior secondary division of this year's Hong Kong Student Science Project Competition, he encouraged young people to draw inspiration from everyday life and consider how to make the city a better place. He said, "The idea is not complicated, but with dedication to putting it into practice, even a small invention can make a big difference. The next invention to reach the world may well come from one of the students here today." The campaign partners of IC 2026 are the Hong Kong Federation of Youth Groups and the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation. Meanwhile, over 40 programme partners, including local universities, R&D centres and government departments, are supporting the carnival by setting up booths at the Hong Kong Science Park, showcasing a series of I&T achievements and providing interactive games. Besides, about 150 workshops and over 10 webinars across various subjects including aerospace technology and AI will be held during the carnival. All IC 2026 activities are free of charge. Some of the activities require pre-registration. Details are available on the thematic webpage ( innocarnival.hk ). Places are limited and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. Members of the public are most welcome to join. During the carnival, free shuttle bus services will be provided between the Hong Kong Science Park and various districts, including MTR University Station, Tai Wai Station, Kowloon Tong Station, and Admiralty Station, with new routes added this year to Yuen Long Station and Tseung Kwan O Station, offering convenient access for visitors.

items.title: Hong Kong Customs detects two drug trafficking cases involving incoming passengers at airport (with photos)
items.description: Hong Kong Customs for two consecutive days (October 23 and 24) detected two drug trafficking cases involving incoming passengers at Hong Kong International Airport and seized about 5 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds and 5.4kg of suspected cocaine, with a total estimated market value of about $4.37 million. In the first case, a 37-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong, China from Bangkok, Thailand, via Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam yesterday (October 23). During customs clearance, Customs officers found about 5kg of suspected cannabis buds inside his check-in baggage. He was subsequently arrested. In the second case, a 46-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong, China from Sao Paulo, Brazil, via Zurich, Switzerland, today (October 24). During customs clearance, Customs officers found about 5.4kg of suspected cocaine inside his check-in baggage. He was subsequently arrested. The arrested men have each been charged with one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug. The two cases will be brought up at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on October 26. Customs will continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking activities through intelligence analysis. The department also reminds members of the public to stay alert and not participate in drug trafficking activities for monetary return. They must not accept hiring or delegation from another party to carry controlled items into and out of Hong Kong. They are also reminded not to carry unknown items for other people. Customs will continue to apply a risk assessment approach and focus on selecting passengers from high-risk regions for clearance to combat transnational drug trafficking activities. Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment. Members of the public may report any suspected drug trafficking activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form ( eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: Counter Terrorism Education Thematic Exhibition opens today (with photos)
items.description: An opening ceremony was held today (October 24) at the Hong Kong Museum of History in Tsim Sha Tsui to mark the launch of the Counter Terrorism Education Thematic Exhibition. The exhibition is organised by the Inter-departmental Counter Terrorism Unit (ICTU), co-organised by the National Security Department of the Hong Kong Police Force, and coordinated by the Security Bureau. Through multimedia displays and interactive experiences, the exhibition aims to enhance public awareness of counter-terrorism (CT) and strengthen public response capabilities. Addressing the opening ceremony, the Secretary for Security, Mr Tang Ping-keung, emphasised that terrorism knows no borders. Hong Kong must therefore remain vigilant and be prepared for potential threats, while continuing to strengthen its CT capabilities in the area of prevention, preparedness, response and recovery. Mr Tang said the exhibition aims to deepen public understanding of terrorism, the global CT landscape, and Hong Kong’s CT strategies. It also seeks to encourage members of the public to stay alert and embrace the message that “greater vigilance means lower risk”, working together to safeguard Hong Kong’s security. Other officiating guests included the Commissioner of Police, Mr Chow Yat-ming, and the Secretary General of the Committee for Safeguarding National Security of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), Mr Au Chi-kwong. Representatives from the six disciplined services member departments of the ICTU and their youth groups also attended the opening ceremony. The CT thematic exhibition is being staged in the main lobby on the first floor of the Hong Kong Museum of History. Together with the National Security Exhibition Gallery on the second floor, it creates a complementary and synergistic exhibition experience. The exhibition is open to the public from today until March 1 next year. The thematic exhibition features diverse and vibrant content across multiple zones, showcasing the global and local CT landscape; Hong Kong’s CT strategies, including the Three-tier Prevention Framework for CT established by the HKSAR Government and the city’s CT legal framework; as well as the CT roles of the ICTU and other government departments. Interactive highlights include the “Spot and Report” and “Run, Hide, Report” games, together with an authentic wartime bomb weighing over 1 000 pounds, dismantled in 2014 and provided for display by the Police Explosive Ordnance Disposal Bureau. The exhibition enables visitors to gain CT and emergency preparedness knowledge through immersive and interactive experiences, thereby enhancing public awareness of terrorism prevention. In addition, the “Safe Community Plus+”, jointly organised by the ICTU and the Hong Kong Federation of Youth Groups for a third time, was officially launched following the opening ceremony. Over the next six months, the “Safe Community Plus+” will visit various schools and community venues, using a variety of interactive mini-games to help students and members of the public to learn about security awareness and emergency response in an engaging manner. Looking ahead, the HKSAR Government will, in line with the direction set out in the Hong Kong’s First Five-year Plan and the Chief Executive’s 2026 Policy Address, continue to monitor the global terrorism trends and CT measures, further strengthen specialised CT training, optimise various contingency plans, deepen cross-boundary and international cooperation and exchanges, as well as expand community intelligence networks, with a view to comprehensively enhancing Hong Kong’s overall CT planning and preparedness, and strengthening its CT governance capabilities.

items.title: Security Bureau Youth Uniformed Group Leaders Forum holds induction course to commence training activities (with photos)
items.description: The Security Bureau (SB) today (October 24) began a two-day-one-night induction course for members of the new-term SB Youth Uniformed Group Leaders Forum to launch training activities in the coming year for Hong Kong youth members and those from its partners, Shenzhen University and youth groups of public security forces of Macao. Addressing the launch ceremony, the Secretary for Security, Mr Tang Ping-keung, introduced activities in the coming year and shared four key factors for success. He encouraged youth members to acquire knowledge across different fields, sharpen their communication and analytical skills, maintain an attitude to learn through practical application and establish a holistic outlook. He said that future development opportunities for young people are unlimited and encouraged members to seize the chances to broaden their horizons through next year's activities, nurture an affection for home and country, cultivate a global vision and service spirit, and translate what they have learnt into capital to contribute to the country. Leaders from Leaders Forum's partners, the Vice President of Shenzhen University, Professor Li Meng, and the Director of the Academy of Public Security Forces of Macao, Mr Wong Chi-fai, also delivered speeches at the launch ceremony. The induction course was held at the Fire and Ambulance Services Academy in Hong Kong. In addition to discipline, team-building and leadership training, the youth members also experienced simulation training of firemen and ambulancemen. Moreover, distinguished personalities from different sectors were invited to share their experiences in the induction course, including the Permanent President of the Leaders Forum, Mr Chan Hak-kan, who provided an analysis of irreplaceable skills in the AI era; and Hong Kong's female wushu athlete Juanita Mok, who shared her journey in learning wushu. Teacher of College of Social Sciences of Shenzhen University Mr Gao Wang and the Acting Director of the Research and Development Department of the Academy of Public Security Forces of Macao, Mr Un Kim-fong, also gave talks at thematic seminars. The SB established the Leaders Forum in October 2022 to deepen participation in youth work. There are 50 members from Hong Kong, 30 youths from Shenzhen University and 26 members from the youth groups of public security forces of Macao in the new term of the Leaders Forum.

items.title: SCST congratulates Hong Kong, China athletes on winning five more medals today in Asian Para Games
items.description: The Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism, Miss Rosanna Law, today (October 24) extended her congratulations to boccia athletes Leung Yuk-wing and Cheung Yuen on winning a gold medal in Mixed Pairs-BC4 at the 5th Asian Para Games, bringing the Hong Kong, China delegation its third gold medal of the Games. Miss Law also congratulated fencing athletes Chung Yuen-ping, Lam Ka-man, Tong Nga-ting and Yu Chui-yee on winning a silver medal in Women's Sabre Team; then Lam Ka-man and Tong Nga-ting together with Glass Sean and Kwong Yuen-hing on winning a bronze medal in Sabre Mixed Team; boccia athletes Loung John, Chan Pak-lun and Yeung Hiu-lam on winning a bronze medal in Mixed Team-BC1/BC2; and boccia athletes Tse Tak-wah and Chan Ho-yan on winning a bronze medal in Mixed Pairs-BC3. Miss Law said, "Hong Kong, China athletes continued their winning streak on the final day of the Asian Para Games, adding five more medals and bringing glory to Hong Kong. Being the top spot pair in the world ranking, Leung Yuk-wing and Cheung Yuen displayed exceptional skills, winning four consecutive rounds in the final to secure the gold medal. Loung John, Chan Pak-lun, Yeung Hiu-lam, Tse Tak-wah and Chan Ho-yan performed admirably, winning two bronze medals. The boccia team achieved their best result ever, taking home two gold, three silver, and three bronze medals. Chung Yuen-ping, Lam Ka-man, Tong Nga-ting, Yu Chui-yee, Glass Sean and Kwong Yuen-hing played to win, adding another silver and one bronze medals to the fencing team's tally. The fencing team has now won a total of eight medals, with three silver and five bronze medals, surpassing their previous performance. I sincerely thank all the athletes for their hard work, and the coaches, medical team, and support staff for their dedicated assistance. This honour belongs to the entire team, making all Hong Kong citizens moved and proud!" The Hong Kong, China Delegation has so far won 41 medals, namely three gold, 14 silver and 24 bronze medals, at the Asian Para Games. items.title: CE congratulates Hong Kong, China athletes on achievements at 5th Asian Para Games
items.description: The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, today (October 24) congratulated Hong Kong, China athletes on their remarkable achievements at the 5th Asian Para Games and commended them for their outstanding performance and noble sportsmanship. Mr Lee said, "The Hong Kong, China delegation delivered an excellent performance at this year's Asian Para Games, winning a total of 41 medals, comprising 3 gold medals, 14 silver medals and 24 bronze medals, and achieving the best-ever historical result in boccia with a total of 2 gold, 3 silver, and 3 bronze medals. These heartening achievements have written a splendid chapter in the development of para sports in Hong Kong. "Hong Kong, China athletes gave their utmost in the competition, demonstrating superb skills and indomitable determination. Their achievements have not only brought honour to Hong Kong, but also inspired the community with their perseverance and never-give-up sportsmanship. Their outstanding performance has earned the admiration and pride of the entire Hong Kong community. "The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government has always attached great importance to sports development for persons with disabilities, helping them to realise their potential and pursue their dreams. Through the Hong Kong Sports Institute, the Government provides full-time high-level training for elite athletes with disabilities, enabling them to receive professional coaching with access to barrier-free world-class training venues and equipment, and comprehensive support in sports science and sport medicine, helping them represent Hong Kong, China in competitions in the Mainland and abroad. With effect from April 1, 2025, the Government raised the level of direct financial support for elite athletes with disabilities across the board, and for the first time introduced a Senior Squad funding tier. Together with the existing elite tiers, it further enhances the training pathway. The outstanding performance at this year's Asian Para Games demonstrates that our policy direction is on the right track. "I would like to thank all the athletes, coaches, medical teams and support personnel for their tireless efforts and dedication. The Government will continue to work closely with the China Hong Kong Paralympic Committee, the Hong Kong Sports Institute and various national sports associations to devote resources to nurturing talent, helping more athletes with disabilities unleash their potential, surpass themselves and achieve new levels in future international competitions."

items.title: Suspected unauthorised use of email account of DH's HIV Testing Service website, involving no data loss or leakage
items.description: The Department of Health (DH) said today (October 24) that the email account for its HIV Testing Service website ( www.hivtest.gov.hk ) was suspected of being misused, with emails and text messages (SMS) sent to the public under the guise of the DH, claiming that the recipients are exposed to Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), and should seek medical advice and get tested as soon as possible. The DH is conducting a thorough investigation into the incident and has not yet found any evidence of data loss or leakage. The DH emphasised that these emails and SMS messages were not sent by the DH, nor does the DH notify individuals in this manner. Members of the public who receive suspicious emails or SMS should not click on any links contained therein or provide personal information. Anyone who has provided personal information to suspicious individuals or suspects they have been scammed should contact the Police. Upon discovering the incident last night, DH staff immediately conducted a comprehensive inspection of the network system with the outsourced service provider and investigated the incident overnight. So far, no data loss or leakage has been detected. The DH reported the incident to the Police and notified the Digital Policy Office. The HIV Testing Service website will be suspended starting today until cybersecurity experts have conducted a comprehensive investigation and review to confirm that there are no security risks to the system. While the website is suspended, members of the public may still call the Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome Hotline (2780 2211) to arrange a free, anonymous and confidential HIV antibody test. The Government has always attached great importance to cybersecurity. The DH has also been conducting regular information security risk assessments, and will continue to review and enhance existing security measures to keep relevant measures abreast of the times in order to safeguard network and system security.

items.title: Speech by CS at 10th Anniversary Retitling Banquet of EdUHK (English only) (with photos/video)
items.description: Following is the speech by the Chief Secretary for Administration, Mr Chan Kwok-ki, at the 10th Anniversary Retitling Banquet of the Education University of Hong Kong (EdUHK) today (October 23): 尊敬的王劍參贊 (Director-General of the International Department of the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Mr Wang Jian), Dr David Wong (Chairman of the Council of EdUHK), Professor John Lee (President of EdUHK), faculty, staff, students and alumni of the EdUHK, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, Good evening. It is a great honour to be here with you tonight at this landmark celebration. This evening, we are proud to mark the 10th anniversary of the EdUHK's retitling. Much more than just a name change, the school's retitling was a big step forward. It opened a bright new chapter for this University and for Hong Kong. Over the past decade, the EdUHK has evolved into a dynamic, education-focused university with a diversity of academic strengths. It has earned worldwide recognition in many ways. This year, the QS World University Rankings by Subject ranked EdU seventh in the world and second in Asia. And in the 2026 Times Higher Education Sustainability Impact Ratings, EdU placed second in Quality Education, one of the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals. When it comes to talent, EdU is showing the way. This year, 73 EdU scholars were named among the World's Top 2% Scientists, a ranking compiled by Stanford University. Since 2018, EdU researchers have won 265 awards at major international invention exhibitions. These achievements show that EdU leads in quality education, while highlighting its growing impact in sustainable development and academic excellence. I am also delighted to hear that nearly 50 EdU student athletes and alumni took part in the recent Asian Games. They won 15 medals - two gold and three silver. They helped Hong Kong win a record number of medals at the Asian Games. Ladies and gentlemen, the National 15th Five-Year Plan, launched earlier this year, supports Hong Kong in better integrating into, and serving, the nation's overall development. And Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, launched last month, puts a priority on the integrated development of education, technology and talent. EdU's development strategy is built on "Education Futures, Diverse Talents". It draws on its traditional strengths, while equipping students with a wide range of skills. I am pleased to say this matches the Government's long-term vision perfectly. EdU is Hong Kong's leading university for teacher education and lifelong learning, and it is expanding its academic offerings, adding programmes covering psychology, data science, sociology, sports science, new media and other disciplines. All 13 of its Bachelor of Education programmes are now double-degree programmes, giving students – tomorrow's teachers – broader learning opportunities. The Government is just as committed to creating opportunities. We want Hong Kong to rise as an international education hub. And the Northern Metropolis University Town is our flagship initiative. The University Town, totalling some 1 000 hectares, will bring together education, technology and talent, driving integrated development among Government, academia, industries, research and investment sectors. Just as important, the University Town and the larger Northern Metropolis will greatly expand our connectivity with the Greater Bay Area. In this area, EdU is already moving ahead. This year, it set up the EdUHK Shenzhen Research Institute and the Shenzhen Educational Development Centre. As Dr Wong said a few minutes ago, this is "a historic milestone in EdU's expansion into the Greater Bay Area". EdU's first decade as a university has built a strong foundation – for its students and teachers, for Hong Kong and our future as an international education hub. I am confident it will create lasting value here in Hong Kong, across the country and around the world. Once again, a happy 10th anniversary to the EdUHK, and to everyone who has played a part in its remarkable decade of progress. Thank you.

items.title: CHP records case of severe paediatric influenza infection
items.description: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 23) recorded a severe case of paediatric influenza infection. The CHP urged the public not to underestimate the seasonal influenza and to receive vaccinations as early as possible, especially those in high-risk groups, to protect their own health and that of their families. In addition, the public should maintain good personal and environmental hygiene at all times to prevent influenza and other respiratory illnesses. The case involves a 3-year-old boy with underlying health conditions. He developed a fever and cough on October 20. He experienced mild shortness of breath the next day and was taken to a private clinic for treatment. On October 22, his condition worsened, and he was brought to the Accident and Emergency Department of Tuen Mun Hospital. He briefly lost consciousness, but was resuscitated and was admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU). His respiratory specimen tested positive for influenza A (H1) virus. The clinical diagnosis was influenza A infection complicated with asthma exacerbation, acute necrotising encephalopathy and septic shock. The patient remains hospitalised and is in critical condition. The CHP's preliminary investigation revealed that the boy travelled to the United States during the incubation period and had not received the 2026/27 Seasonal Influenza Vaccination (SIV). One of his close contacts recently developed mild upper respiratory symptoms that did not require hospitalisation and has recovered. The CHP will continue to investigate the case. "Hong Kong entered the influenza season in late June this year and the influenza season has lasted for nearly four months by now. Currently, local influenza activity remains at a high level. Over the past four weeks (from September 20 to October 17), the percentage of respiratory specimens testing positive for seasonal influenza viruses remained between 10.04 to 11.61 per cent. During the same period, the influenza admission rate in public hospitals also remained between 0.46 and 0.67 cases per 10 000 population. Both indicators were above the respective baseline thresholds of 4.94 per cent and 0.27 cases per 10 000 population. A cumulative total of 26 cases of severe paediatric influenza infection have been recorded in the current influenza season. Among these cases, 20 patients have recovered and been discharged from hospital, two are in serious condition, two are in critical condition, and two have passed away," said the Controller of the CHP, Dr Edwin Tsui. "Vaccine effectiveness begins to wane approximately nine months after vaccination. Therefore, the World Health Organization recommends receiving SIV every year. For most people, more than nine months have passed since they received last season's (2025/26) SIV. Hence, a decline in protection is inevitable. A decline in the overall population's herd immunity, coupled with the fact that the current influenza season has persisted at high levels for an extended period, has increased the likelihood of infection and severe complications among high-risk groups. Receiving SIV is the most effective way to prevent severe cases of seasonal influenza and its complications. SIV also reduces the risk of hospitalisation and death. The CHP's analysis of data from the previous year revealed that the rate of severe complications or death among unvaccinated children following influenza infection was approximately five times higher than that among vaccinated children. Among unvaccinated residents aged 65 years or older living in residential care homes for the elderly, the rate of severe complications was approximately four times higher than that among vaccinated residents. Therefore, all people aged 6 months or above, except those with known contraindications, should receive SIV for personal protection as early as possible," he added. The 2026/27 SIV programmes, including the SIV School Outreach Programme (SIVSOP), commenced on September 17. The SIVSOP this year has introduced a new Electronic Consent Form (e-consent form) feature via eHealth. This new measure not only enables the public to join the SIV Programmes but also streamlines the administrative procedures for healthcare service providers and schools, so that SIV outreach activities can start as early as possible. About 1 000 schools have organised SIV outreach activities. SIV outreach activities are expected to be completed by mid-December, about two weeks earlier than last year. The health condition of children with influenza can deteriorate rapidly. Parents must pay close attention to their condition and visit an accident and emergency department immediately if the child's condition deteriorates with symptoms such as shortness of breath, wheezing, blue lips, chest pain, confusion, a persistent fever or convulsions. Members of the public should seek medical attention as soon as possible if they develop respiratory symptoms. If they live with members of high-risk groups, such as children, the elderly and those with underlying illnesses or compromised immune systems, they should wear a surgical mask at home to reduce the risk of infecting them. Other effective ways to reduce the spread of the disease include maintaining household hygiene, frequently cleaning and disinfecting frequently touched surfaces, practising good hand hygiene, and ensuring proper indoor air circulation. Members of the public may refer to the CHP's COVID-19 & Flu Express , Seasonal Influenza Webpage and Vaccination Schemes for the latest information.

items.title: Tuen Mun Hospital Neuroscience Centre opens, providing efficient and innovative integrated neuromedicine services (with photos/video)
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hospital Authority: ​The opening ceremony of the Tuen Mun Hospital Neuroscience Centre (the Centre) was held today (October 23). The Centre introduces multidisciplinary, efficient and innovative integrated treatment and rehabilitation services for patients suffering from neurological diseases. The Secretary for Health, Professor Lo Chung-mau, accompanied by the Hospital Authority (HA) Chairman, Mr Henry Fan; the HA Chief Executive, Dr Libby Lee; and the New Territories West Cluster Chief Executive, Dr Deacons Yeung, visited the Centre and learned about the Centre's operations and latest developments. They also met with a patient who received Magnetic Resonance-guided Focused Ultrasound (MRgFUS) treatment at the Centre to understand his treatment and rehabilitation progress. Professor Lo said, "The Chief Executive's 2022 Policy Address proposed the establishment of the Tuen Mun Hospital Neuroscience Centre, with phased services commencing from the end of 2024. Through proactive cross-specialty collaboration and service integration, alongside the introduction of advanced technologies, the Centre brings hope to patients suffering from acute stroke and dyskinesia. Looking forward, I expect the Centre to engage more specialties and expand its core services to provide more comprehensive care for patients." The Centre provides one-stop, safe and efficient integrated neuromedicine services, introducing Hong Kong's first MRgFUS and Intraoperative Magnetic Resonance Imaging services. These advancements offer more advanced treatment options and enhance outcomes for patients with neurological diseases. The Centre adopts the "Programme Floor" concept, integrating advanced technology operating theatres, wards, and day services on the same floor to facilitate multidisciplinary team collaboration and provide convenience to patients by saving their time required to visit multiple departments. Mr Fan stated that the "Programme Floor" approach implemented in the Tuen Mun Hospital Neuroscience Centre enabled multidisciplinary teams to provide one-stop and continuous care to patients with neurological diseases. The HA has introduced various advanced technologies in the Centre, which best demonstrate the patient-centric approach. The HA will continue to devote resources to promoting the development of neuroscience and to provide better healthcare services to the public. The Centre is planning to establish an Integrated Rehabilitation Centre to ensure patients receive multidisciplinary support from the acute phase of the disease to rehabilitation training, enhancing their ability in self-care and enabling faster community reintegration. In addition to upgrading facilities and optimising services, the Centre will actively advance scientific research collaboration with institutions, aiming to bring more innovative and effective treatments to patients with neurological diseases.

precise risk assessments: carrying out intensive and targeted mosquito control work at locations with more serious mosquito infestations, including stepping up inspections, eliminating mosquito breeding and potential breeding grounds, applying larvicides, conducting fogging operations to eradicate adult mosquitoes, and placing mosquito trapping devices at appropriate locations; promotion and education: organising exhibitions with relevant departments and stakeholders, and distributing leaflets and posters to enhance public awareness of mosquito control and prevention; and rapid alert mechanism: notifying residential estates that have subscribed to the gravidtrap Rapid Alert System, and advising property management companies and residents to stay vigilant and work together in taking mosquito prevention and elimination measures. During the follow-up actions and following the discovery of stagnant water or stagnant water containers at a public housing estate in Kwai Tsing District and a park in Yuen Long District, the FEHD has issued three statutory notices to the responsible persons-in-charge, requiring the clearance of such items within a specified timeframe. Public participation is crucial to the effective control of mosquito problems. The FEHD appeals to members of the public to continue to work together in strengthening personal mosquito control measures, including: tidying up their premises and checking for any accumulation of water inside the premises; removing all unnecessary water collections and eliminating the sources; checking household items (those placed in outdoor and open areas in particular), such as refuse containers, vases, air conditioner drip trays, and laundry racks to prevent stagnant water; changing water in flower vases and scrubbing their inner surfaces thoroughly, and removing water in saucers under potted plants at least once a week; properly covering all containers that hold water to prevent mosquitoes from accessing the water; properly disposing of articles that can contain water, such as disposable meal boxes and empty cans; and scrubbing drains and surface sewers with alkaline detergent at least once a week to remove any mosquito eggs. Starting in August 2025, following the completion of the surveillance of individual survey areas, and once the latest gravidtrap index and the density index are available, the FEHD has been disseminating relevant information through press releases, its website and social media. It aims to allow members of the public to quickly grasp the mosquito infestation situation and strengthen mosquito control efforts, thereby reducing the risk of chikungunya fever (CF) transmission. ​Following recommendations from the World Health Organization and taking into account the local situation in Hong Kong, the FEHD sets up gravidtraps in districts where mosquito-borne diseases have been recorded in the past, as well as in densely populated places such as housing estates, hospitals and schools to monitor the breeding and distribution of Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, which can transmit CF and dengue fever. At present, the FEHD has set up gravidtraps in 62 survey areas of the community, with a surveillance period of two weeks. During the surveillance period, the FEHD will collect the gravidtraps once a week. After the first week of surveillance, the FEHD will immediately examine the glue boards inside the retrieved gravidtraps for the presence of adult Aedine mosquitoes to compile the Gravidtrap Index (First Phase) and Density Index (First Phase). At the end of the second week of surveillance, the FEHD will instantly check the glue boards for the presence of adult Aedine mosquitoes. Data from the two weeks of surveillance will be combined to obtain the Area Gravidtrap Index and the Area Density Index. The Gravidtrap and Density indexes for Aedes albopictus in different survey areas, as well as information on mosquito prevention and control measures, are available on the department's webpage ( www.fehd.gov.hk/english/pestcontrol/dengue_fever/Dengue_Fever_Gravidtrap_Index_Update.html# ).

items.title: Hong Kong Customs detects case involving precious metals and stones dealer carrying out specified cash transaction without Category B registration
items.description: Hong Kong Customs yesterday (October 22) detected a case involving a local company that conducted cash transactions of watches containing precious metals and stones valued at over HK$120,000 while not being a Category B registrant under the Dealers in Precious Metals and Stones Regulatory Regime. The investigation is ongoing. According to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), unless exempted, any person who is seeking to carry on a business of dealing in precious metals and stones and engage in any transaction(s) (whether making or receiving a payment) with a total value at or above HK$120,000 in Hong Kong is required to register with Hong Kong Customs. In particular, no person other than a Category B registrant may carry out a cash transaction with a total value at or above HK$120,000 in the course of business of dealing in precious metals and stones. Any dealer who is not a Category B registrant, who claims to be a Category B registrant, claims to be authorised to carry out, or carries out any cash transaction(s) with a total value at or above HK$120,000, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a maximum fine of HK$100,000 and imprisonment for six months. Customs reminds dealers in precious metals and stones that they must obtain the relevant registration before they can carry out any cash or non-cash transaction(s) with a total value at or above HK$120,000. For the forms, procedures and guidelines to submit applications for registration, please visit the website for Dealers in Precious Metals and Stones Registration System ( www.drs.customs.gov.hk ) or Customs' webpage ( www.customs.gov.hk/en/service-enforcement-information/anti-money-laundering/supervision-of-dealers-in-precious-metals-and-ston/index.html ). Members of the public may report any suspected transactions involving precious metals and stones with a total value at or above HK$120,000 conducted without the required registration to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form ( eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: Family Council's Primary School Roving Interactive Drama Series premieres successfully today (with photos)
items.description: The Primary School Roving Interactive Drama Series, jointly held by the Home and Youth Affairs Bureau (HYAB) and the Family Council, premiered at Yaumati Catholic Primary School (Hoi Wang Road) this afternoon (October 23), with approximately 350 students and parents in attendance. The Family Council adopted "Family: Harmony and Inclusivity" as this year's publicity campaign theme, aiming to foster the acceptance of diversity, cultural inclusion and intergenerational harmony within families, and further promote positive family values ​​in the community, thereby building a harmonious and inclusive society while reinforcing the role of the family as the cornerstone of society. Focused on the theme of "Family: Harmony and Inclusivity", the Primary School Roving Interactive Drama Series depicts the experiences and growth journey of the But's Family as they take part in the Spinning Top Competition for Primary Schools. The characters in the drama evolve from pursuing only victory to gradually learning to listen, empathise, and take responsibility; and from fearing failure to being willing to try and embrace self-affirmation. The experiences portray the power of family members standing by and supporting one another. Traditional Chinese virtues such as propriety, righteousness, integrity, shamefulness, love and benevolence, as well as peace and inclusion, are woven throughout the entire drama. Through diverse and interactive approaches, the drama allows the audience to step into the characters' situations and experience the importance of mutual respect and building consensus. The drama also highlights the importance of family strength, emphasising how the support and inclusivity of family members serve as a steadfast foundation when facing adversity. It also encourages the audience, especially young people, to practise virtues and demonstrate a spirit of benevolence, mutual support and positivity. Speaking at the premiere, the Commissioner for Women Affairs of the HYAB, Ms Joyce Chan , said that the interactive drama blends traditional virtues with creativity, aiming to spark audience's interest and resonance. Besides promoting good family virtues, she also expressed her hope that the drama could inspire parents to guide their children towards positive, proactive and self-reliant values from an early age. Ms Chan also mentioned that the Chief Executive announced in the 2026 Policy Address that the HYAB and the Family Council will organise the Hong Kong Excellent Family Awards again to promote good family values to the general public, inherit good family culture and virtues, and continuously inject positive energy into society. Delivering a speech at the event, the Chairperson of the Family Council, Ms Melissa Pang, said that the interactive drama aims to promote the importance of traditional virtues, harmony and inclusivity to the younger generation, allowing positive family values to take root in households, extend to schools, and enrich society. The interactive drama series will tour primary schools across Hong Kong, with around 70 performances staged from this month until March next year, promoting the strength of family and a culture of harmony and inclusivity to students.

items.title: Two incoming passengers convicted and jailed for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes (with photos)
items.description: Two incoming passengers were sentenced to four weeks' to six months' imprisonment with a fine of $2,000 to $4,000 by the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts today (October 23) for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes and failing to declare them to Customs officers, in contravention of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO) (Cap. 109). One of them was also found to be importing alternative smoking products, in contravention of the Import and Export Ordinance (IEO) (Cap. 60). Customs officers intercepted a 39-year-old incoming Mainland male passenger at Hong Kong International Airport on October 21, and seized 181 duty-not-paid cigarettes and 21 600 alternative smoking products from his personal baggage. The estimated market value of the seizures is about $83,000 with a duty potential of about $600. He was immediately arrested, and was sentenced to four weeks' imprisonment with a fine of $4,000 today. Customs officers also intercepted a 31-year-old incoming Mainland male passenger at Hong Kong International Airport yesterday (October 22), and seized about 73 000 duty-not-paid cigarettes, with an estimated market value of about $330,000 and a duty potential of about $240,000, from his personal baggage. He was also immediately arrested, and was sentenced to six months' imprisonment with a fine of $2,000 today. Customs welcomes the sentences. The custodial sentences have imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflect the seriousness of the offences. Customs reminds members of the public and travellers that under the DCO, anyone involved in importing, dealing with, possession of, selling or buying illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Additionally, under the IEO, any person who imports an alternative smoking product into Hong Kong commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form ( eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: Opening remarks by DSJ at seminar "Iteration and Assurance: Cross-Border Arbitration Practice under the New PRC Arbitration Law and the Amendment to the Hong Kong Arbitration Ordinance" of Hong Kong Arbitration Week 2026 (English only) (with photo)
items.description: Following are the opening remarks by the Deputy Secretary for Justice, Dr Cheung Kwok-kwan, at the seminar "Iteration and Assurance: Cross-Border Arbitration Practice under the New PRC Arbitration Law and the Amendment to the Hong Kong Arbitration Ordinance" of the Hong Kong Arbitration Week 2026 today (October 23): Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, Good afternoon. It is my pleasure to join you today during the Hong Kong Arbitration Week 2026 for this seminar on the theme of "Iteration and Assurance: Cross-Border Arbitration Practice under the New PRC Arbitration Law and the Amendment to the Hong Kong Arbitration Ordinance". As global trade and investment flourish, navigating commercial disputes becomes an inevitable feature of cross-border commerce. In this dynamic landscape, arbitration serves as a critical tool that offers a neutral, flexible and internationally enforceable mechanism to resolve cross-border disputes. To remain effective, however, our arbitration framework must stay responsive to the changing needs of international trade. Today's seminar is therefore very timely, as we examine major arbitration legislative advancements taking shape on both sides of the border. New Arbitration Law of People's Republic of China The landmark revision to the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (PRC) came into effect in March this year. This represents the first comprehensive overhaul of the Chinese Mainland arbitral legal framework, aligning it more closely with international standards. Notably, the law introduces a dedicated chapter for foreign-related arbitration. Among its key innovations are provisions permitting ad hoc arbitration for foreign-related maritime disputes and commercial disputes between enterprises within the Pilot Free Trade Zones, the Hainan Free Trade Port, and other designated regions. It also establishes the legal basis for foreign arbitral institutions to set up offices and conduct foreign-related arbitration services in these zones. Furthermore, it explicitly encourages parties to foreign-related disputes to choose arbitral institutions of the PRC, and to choose the PRC as the arbitral seat, both of which include the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Together, these dynamic reforms unlock unprecedented opportunities for Hong Kong's arbitral institutions and practitioners to expand their operational reach in the Chinese Mainland and contribute their international arbitration expertise to foreign-related disputes. Hong Kong arbitration law reform In parallel, Hong Kong is proactively modernising our arbitration legal framework. The Department of Justice (DoJ) established the Working Group on Arbitration Law Reform last year with members drawn from the leading figures of the legal and dispute resolution sector, including Edward (Partner of Haiwen & Partners Hong Kong Office Mr Edward Liu) who will be moderating today's panel discussion shortly. Based on the Working Group's deep-dive examination of Hong Kong's Arbitration Ordinance, the DoJ has formulated amendment proposals under four vital pillars: speed and convenience, confidentiality, scope, as well as fairness and justice. A one-month stakeholder consultation is now underway and will run until October 27. After considering the stakeholders' feedback, the DoJ will take forward the legislative amendments and will strive to complete the exercise within next year. Through these statutory refinements, we hope to offer global users a modern, transparent and forward-looking legal environment for them to choose Hong Kong as their arbitral seat with sheer confidence. Hong Kong's strategic role as a premier dispute resolution hub Anchored in "one country, two systems", Hong Kong's robust framework and dispute resolution ecosystem serve as a solid foundation to support both national and international development. As emphasised in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan (First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030)) and the Policy Address 2026, the Government is committed to deepening Hong Kong's development as an international legal and dispute resolution services centre. As a "super connector" and "super value-adder", Hong Kong leverages its unique proximity to the Chinese Mainland alongside a trusted bilingual common law tradition. Reinforced by the deep expertise in both institutional and ad hoc arbitration, our multilingual legal and dispute resolution community offers global investors and Chinese Mainland enterprises an exceptionally professional, efficient and world-class arbitration environment. As landmark arbitration legislative developments unfold in both the Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong, new horizons are opening for the arbitration community to maximise synergy in cross-border arbitration in the region. On this note, I wish you all an engaging and rewarding seminar. Thank you.

items.title: Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK 2026 spotlights three core growth engines: Finance+, AI+, and global expansion (with photos)
items.description: The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and Invest Hong Kong (InvestHK) today (October 23) hosted a press conference and unveiled details of Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK 2026 (HKFW x SMUHK), which will take place from November 2 to 6. The event is expected to welcome more than 45 000 participants from over 120 economies, alongside more than 1 000 speakers, 800 exhibitors and start-ups, as well as over 30 Chinese Mainland and international delegations. Marking the launch of both the National 15th Five-Year Plan and the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) (Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan), HKFW x SMUHK 2026 will highlight financial empowerment, tech innovation, and global expansion as key engines of sustainable business growth. HKFW x SMUHK is organised by the FSTB, the Commerce and Economic Development Bureau and InvestHK, in collaboration with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), and the Insurance Authority (IA). A global innovation platform powered by Finance+ As the Asia-Pacific region's leading financial centre and the world's top-ranked fintech hub in the latest Global Financial Centres Index, Hong Kong provides a strong foundation for advancing the "Finance+" vision. Backed by deep capital markets and global connectivity, the city is powered by a dual financial and technological engine: a robust financial ecosystem provides the capital needed to scale innovation, while technological advancement continues to transform financial services and unlock new sources of growth. The Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Mr Christopher Hui, said, "In tandem with Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address, which set out the blueprint for our city's future development, this year's Hong Kong FinTech Week carries the forward-looking theme 'Fintech Nexus: Bridging the World, Building the Future'. Our position at the forefront of global fintech is not merely rhetorical, but a proven reality on the world stage. As one of the top international financial centres globally and a leading force in Asia, Hong Kong continues to make confident strides in expanding its fintech capability." He added that the event will showcase how Hong Kong's fintech capability is boosting the city's development in gold and commodity markets, thus linking the international markets with Asia's liquidity. AI+ and a thriving start-up ecosystem empowering innovation As Hong Kong advances its "AI+" agenda for cross‑industry AI deep integration, it stands as a global launch pad for innovators to commercialise and scale technology. Supported by a thriving ecosystem of over 5 200 startups and ongoing development of the Northern Metropolis, Hong Kong opens new global growth pathways, while the world‑topping Shenzhen‑Hong Kong‑Guangzhou innovation cluster demonstrates how aligned research, talent, capital and industry drive innovation and business expansion. Complementing HKFW x SMUHK 2026, the Global Fast Track programme will once again serve as a launch pad for high-growth start-ups and scale-ups seeking to accelerate commercialisation and international expansion. This year's programme has already attracted more than 700 applications from Hong Kong, the Chinese Mainland, wider Asia, Europe, North America, the Middle East, Africa and Oceania. Going global driven by financial empowerment and tech innovation As businesses increasingly look beyond their home markets for growth, Hong Kong serves as a trusted launch pad for international expansion. Retaining first place in the Asian Cities Internationality Index 2026, the city combines global connectivity, international business networks and market access, enabling companies to forge global partnerships and expand internationally. The Director-General of Investment Promotion, Ms Alpha Lau, said, "As HKFW x SMUHK enters its second decade, Hong Kong begins a new chapter with its First Five-Year Plan, unveiled alongside the 2026 Policy Address. This year's three engines - "Finance+", "AI+" and global expansion - reflect the city's strategic priorities: driving innovation and economic development, transforming industries, and enabling multi-market growth. Hong Kong connects these forces, and this year's event will bring together global innovators, investors and enterprises to scale internationally and seize new opportunities through our city." As Hong Kong cements its status as Asia's premier hub for two-way investment, this year's event will welcome over 30 delegations from the Chinese Mainland, including those from Beijing, Jiangsu, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Zhuhai, alongside delegations from North America, Europe, the Gulf Cooperation Council regions, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, Central Asia, and other emerging markets. Their vote of confidence reinforces Hong Kong's standing as Asia's premier platform for companies seeking global expansion. Global visionaries set to take the stage The HKFW x SMUHK 2026 main conference will specifically take place on November 2 and 3 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. It will feature 10 dedicated forums, including the Policy and Visionary Forum, AI & DeepTech Forum, Digital Assets and Web3 Forum, AI in Finance Forum, China-Global Innovation Forum, InsurTech and HealthTech Forum, GreenTech Forum, Founder and Startup Venture Forum, Tech Builder Forum, and Creator Forum. items.title: SCOLAR 30th Anniversary Celebration Ceremony held today (with photos)
items.description: The Standing Committee on Language Education and Research (SCOLAR) 30th Anniversary Celebration Ceremony was held today (October 23). Under the theme "30 Years On: Empowering Language Capabilities for Tomorrow", the ceremony looked back on SCOLAR's journey and achievements in promoting biliteracy and trilingualism, and the development of language education, while also looking ahead to future directions. Officiating at the ceremony, the Acting Secretary for Education, Dr Sze Chun-fai, noted that five universities in Hong Kong have been ranked among the global top 100 in the latest global university rankings released by international higher education institutions, making Hong Kong one of the cities with the highest density of elite institutions worldwide. This achievement not only reflects the efforts of higher education institutions but is also inseparable from the solid foundation of language education. The Education Bureau (EDB) has been promoting biliteracy and trilingualism, with the aim of enabling students to write fluently in both Chinese and English, and to communicate confidently in Cantonese, English and Putonghua. The EDB also seeks to leverage Hong Kong's distinctive advantage of enjoying strong support of the motherland and being connected to the world, in order to nurture high-calibre talent who possess both a deep cultural heritage and a broad international perspective for the benefit of the country and society. Dr Sze commended SCOLAR for its three decades of dedication to conducting research and promoting the development of language education in Hong Kong, as well as for providing valuable and professional advice. He also expressed gratitude to schools, teachers and partners from all sectors of the community for their steadfast support over the years in promoting biliteracy and trilingualism. The EDB would continue to work closely with SCOLAR and partners from various sectors to lay a solid foundation in language competency for the next generation, equipping them to actively integrate into and contribute to the nation's overall development, broaden their international horizons and seize future opportunities. The Chairperson of SCOLAR, Dr Anissa Chan, extended sincere appreciation to former chairpersons, past and current members of SCOLAR, as well as partners from education and other sectors for their longstanding support. She said that, over the past three decades, SCOLAR had worked cohesively with various sectors to implement a wide range of initiatives, creating opportunities for people from different backgrounds to learn and use language in response to the needs of society and the development of language education. Looking ahead, SCOLAR will build on the achievements of the past 30 years and continue to uphold the spirit of innovation, partnership and community engagement, collaborating with various sectors to write a new chapter in the development of language education. The celebration featured a rich programme. Through videos and presentations, SCOLAR showcased the achievements of the Scheme on Early Language and Literacy Development in Chinese and English Language of Young Children, the Research and Development Projects, and the International Summit on the Use of AI in Language Learning and Teaching. Student representatives from the Student Language Ambassador (SLA) Programme reflected on their growth journey as SLAs and shared their learning experiences. Winners of competitions sponsored by SCOLAR and community partners delivered impressive performances, demonstrating through their outstanding language proficiency the achievements of SCOLAR's efforts in promoting community participation and language use. During the chit-chat session, SCOLAR's 30th Anniversary Ambassador, Hins Cheung, together with representatives who had participated in SCOLAR's programmes, shared their experiences in learning and using language, showcasing the positive impact of SCOLAR's initiatives. The ceremony was held at the Y Theatre of Youth Square, and was attended by nearly 600 community partners, teachers, parents, and students who had participated in SCOLAR's programmes. items.title: FS calls on central ministries and commissions and visits AI enterprise in Beijing (with photos)
items.description: The Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, began his visit to Beijing today (October 23). In the morning, he called on the China Securities Regulatory Commission and met with its Chairman, Mr Wu Qing. The two sides had a detailed exchange of views on strengthening collaboration between the Mainland and Hong Kong in securities market regulation and development, as well as further deepening mutual market access. The Chief Executive Officer of the Securities and Futures Commission, Ms Julia Leung, also attended the meeting. In the afternoon, Mr Chan called on the Ministry of Commerce (MOC) and met with Assistant Minister of Commerce Mr Yuan Xiaoming, to exchange views on further deepening economic and trade co-operation between the Mainland and Hong Kong. The Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development, Mr Algernon Yau, accompanied Mr Chan at the meeting. In the presence of Mr Chan and Mr Yuan, Mr Yau signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on strengthening the economic and trade co-operation between the Mainland and Hong Kong with the Director-General of the Department of Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao Affairs of the MOC, Mr Sun Yi, and an MOU on strengthening the exchanges and co-operation with free trade zones and ports with the Director-General of the Department of Pilot Free Trade Zone and Free Trade Port of the MOC, Ms He Yongqian, respectively, under the mechanism of the Mainland and Hong Kong Economic and Trade Co-operation Committee.
