Mr Chan thanked the MOC for its continuous strong support for the HKSAR Government's efforts to promote Hong Kong's economic and trade development. He said that the HKSAR Government will leverage the advantages of Hong Kong's internationalised business environment, professional services system and global resources network to further give full play to Hong Kong's dual roles as a "super connector" and a "super value-adder", enhance its competitiveness and international influence, and consolidate its status as an international trade centre, while contributing to the country's high-quality economic development. The Chief Executive announced in the 2026 Policy Address that, following the signing in 2024 of an amendment agreement to further open up the services market of the Mainland under the framework of the Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA), the two sides will sign an MOU to continue jointly pursuing the comprehensive upgrade of CEPA, with a view to deepening co-operation between the service sectors of Hong Kong and the Mainland, as well as further expanding Mainland market access and areas of liberalisation. In the afternoon, Mr Chan also visited an artificial intelligence company and met with its senior management Mr Chan will depart for Hong Kong tomorrow (October 24) morning.

items.title: CHP announces new melioidosis case
items.description: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 23) announced that one new melioidosis case was recorded in the past week (October 16 to 22). The CHP appealed to members of the public to maintain personal and environmental hygiene to prevent melioidosis. The CHP also specifically reminded high-risk groups, including the elderly and people with underlying diseases, to avoid contact with soil or muddy water after typhoons or storms with a view to lowering infection risk. The case involves a 50-year-old female with underlying illnesses. She lives in Wan Chai District. Since September 30, she has had a persistent fever. On October 3, she attended the Accident and Emergency Department of Ruttonjee Hospital and was admitted for treatment. She was found to have liver abscesses after admission. Specimen taken from her liver abscesses tested positive for Burkholderia pseudomallei. The patient is currently in stable condition. The CHP is investigating the infection source of the case. An initial epidemiological investigation revealed that the case is sporadic. No epidemiological linkages have been established between this case and other confirmed cases previously recorded in Hong Kong. Person-to-person transmission and animal-to-human transmission are rare, but the bacteria causing melioidosis can survive in the local environment. Melioidosis is an endemic disease in Hong Kong, and melioidosis cases have been recorded in Hong Kong each year. As of yesterday (October 22), ten melioidosis cases have been recorded in Hong Kong this year. Last year, 21 melioidosis cases were recorded. According to literature, melioidosis cases are more common after typhoons or rainstorms. The bacterium Burkholderia pseudomallei in soil and muddy water may become exposed on the ground after typhoons or rainstorms, and the bacteria could spread more easily with strong winds or rainstorms. As such, the number of melioidosis cases may increase. Where practicable, members of the public should stay indoors during typhoons and rainstorms, avoid travelling to areas with potential flooding, and not wade in or have contact with muddy water and soil. In addition, high-risk individuals should avoid paths near stormwater drains where aerosols may be generated from contaminated water. Members of the public should also take the following preventive measures against infection: Avoid contact with contaminated soil; Wear appropriate protective clothing or footwear when participating in activities with possible contact with soil or water, e.g. using gloves and wearing boots. High-risk individuals may also consider wearing a surgical mask; Wash or shower after exposure to contaminated water or soil; Always clean any wounds as soon as possible and cover them with waterproof dressings; Wash hands with liquid soap and water after handling soil or gardening; Observe food hygiene and avoid drinking raw water; and Travellers can contract the disease through outdoor water sports. Risk of infection can be minimised by avoiding exposure to water sources (such as rivers, ponds or lakes) that might be contaminated. The CHP appealed to members of the public to seek medical advice if they develop symptoms, in particular people with diabetes or other immunocompromising conditions, in order to receive an appropriate medical diagnosis and treatment. For more information on melioidosis, please visit the website of the CHP at www.chp.gov.hk/en/healthtopics/content/24/101110.html .

items.title: Hong Kong Customs detects two drug trafficking cases involving incoming passengers at airport (with photos)
items.description: Hong Kong Customs yesterday (October 22) detected two drug trafficking cases involving incoming passengers at Hong Kong International Airport, and seized about 2 kilograms of suspected cocaine and about 3kg of suspected cannabis buds with an estimated market value of about $1.9 million. Two men were arrested. In the first case, a 25-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Penang, Malaysia, today. During customs clearance, Customs officers found 2kg of suspected cocaine inside his check-in baggage. The man was subsequently arrested. In the second case, a 36-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Phnom Penh, Cambodia, via from Bangkok, Thailand, yesterday. During Customs clearance, Customs officers found 3kg of suspected cannabis buds, two types of products containing suspected Part I poison and 38 sticks of duty-not-paid cigarettes inside his carry-on baggage. The man was subsequently arrested. The arrested man in the first case has been charged with one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug, while the arrested man in the second case has been charged with one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug, one count of possession of dutiable goods, one count of failing to declare to a member of the Customs and Excise Service the possession of dutiable goods and one count of possession of Part I poison. The two cases will be brought up at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts tomorrow (October 24). Customs will continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking activities through intelligence analysis. The department also reminds members of the public to stay alert and not to participate in drug trafficking activities for monetary return. They must not accept hiring or delegation from another party to carry controlled items into and out of Hong Kong. They are also reminded not to carry unknown items for other people. Customs will continue to apply a risk assessment approach and focus on selecting passengers from high-risk regions for clearance to combat transnational drug trafficking activities. Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment. Under the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance, any person who possesses any poison included in Part I of the Poisons List other than in accordance with provisions commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $100,000 and imprisonment for two years. Under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance, cigarettes are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Members of the public may report any suspected drug trafficking activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form ( eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: Update on mosquito-borne diseases, dengue fever and chikungunya fever
items.description: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 23) announced the latest situation regarding dengue fever (DF) and chikungunya fever (CF). Although Hong Kong has entered autumn, the weather has yet to cool down and there are occasional showers, which is favourable for mosquito breeding. Members of the public are reminded to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Dengue fever ---------------- From October 16 to yesterday (October 22), the CHP recorded two imported DF cases. The patients had visited India and Bangladesh respectively during the incubation period. Hong Kong has recorded 36 DF cases so far this year, comprising 34 imported cases and two local cases. A total of 59 DF cases were recorded last year (2025), all of which were imported cases. In 2024, 161 DF cases were recorded, comprising 156 imported cases and five local cases. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the global incidence of DF has markedly increased over the past two decades, posing a substantial public health challenge. In 2024, the WHO recorded over 14 million DF cases, which was a record number. In 2025, over five million cases and over 4 000 DF-related deaths were reported in over 90 countries/territories. From January to September 2026, around 2.5 million cases and over 1 500 DF-related deaths have been recorded globally. DF has long been prevalent in many neighbouring tourist destinations. So far this year, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Sri Lanka and Vietnam each recorded over 100 000 cases; Indonesia recorded over 80 000 cases; India and Malaysia each recorded over 70 000 cases; and Singapore recorded over 2 700 cases. Meanwhile, according to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, as of September, Guangdong Province has recorded 586 cases this year, of which 155 were recorded in September. Detailed information on the latest DF situation in Hong Kong, as well as neighbouring and overseas countries and areas, has been uploaded to the CHP's website . Chikungunya fever ----------------------- From October 16 to yesterday, no new cases of CF had been recorded. Hong Kong has recorded seven confirmed CF cases so far this year, including six imported cases and one local case. Hong Kong recorded a total of 82 confirmed CF cases last year. Among them, 11 were local cases and the rest were imported cases. According to the WHO, a total of 502 264 CF cases and 186 CF-related deaths were reported in 41 countries/territories last year. Cases were reported in the Americas, Africa, Asia and Europe. According to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, Guangdong Province has recorded 1 753 cases this year (as of September). Among them, 1 014 were recorded in September, a sharp increase compared to the number of cases recorded from July to August (171 to 496 cases). Preventive measures to be taken by the public ---------------------------------------------------- The CHP reminds members of the public to maintain good environmental hygiene, and to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Mosquito-borne diseases such as DF and CF are endemic in various countries worldwide. The risk of importation persists. Members of the public should check the situation at their destinations before travelling abroad, especially when travelling to Southeast Asian countries. Additionally, whether travelling or not, members of the public should use DEET-containing insect repellents or other effective active ingredients properly to prevent mosquito bites, but the following precautions should be taken when using them: read the label instructions carefully first; apply right before entering an area with a risk of mosquito bites; apply on exposed skin and clothing; use DEET of up to 30 per cent for pregnant women and up to 10 per cent for children (for children who travel to countries or areas where mosquito-borne diseases are endemic or epidemic, and where exposure is likely, those aged 2 months or above can use DEET-containing insect repellents with a DEET concentration of up to 30 per cent); apply sunscreen first, then insect repellent; reapply only when needed and follow the instructions; and in addition to DEET, there are other insect repellents available on the market containing different active ingredients, such as IR3535 and picaridin. When using any insect repellent, the public should follow the usage instructions and precautions on the product label. ​The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) appeals to members of the public to continue to stay alert and work together to carry out mosquito prevention and control measures early, including inspecting their homes and surroundings to remove potential breeding grounds, changing water in vases and scrubbing their inner surfaces, removing water in saucers under potted plants at least once a week, and properly disposing of containers such as empty cans and lunch boxes. The FEHD also advises members of the public and property management agencies to keep drains free of blockage and level all defective ground surfaces to prevent the accumulation of water. They should also scrub all drains and surface sewers with an alkaline detergent at least once a week to remove any mosquito eggs. ​The public should call 1823 in case of mosquito problems, and may visit the following pages for more information: the CF page of the CHP and the Travel Health Service , the latest Travel Health News , tips for using insect repellents , and the CHP Facebook Page , Instagram Account and YouTube Channel , and also the Mosquito Prevention and Control dedicated page of the FEHD.

items.title: New elements injected to enhance vibrancy of Central (with photos)
items.description: The Development Bureau (DEVB) announced today (October 23) that the first phase of streetscape beautification works for Lan Kwai Fong and streets nearby as announced in the 2025 Policy Address has completed by Halloween as scheduled. Starting from 7pm today (October 23), visitors can enjoy a brand new light art show and a mural created by local street artists in the beautified Lan Kwai Fong, immersing themselves in a unique Halloween atmosphere. A spokesperson for the DEVB said, "The smooth completion of the first phase of the Lan Kwai Fong beautification project was a result of public-private collaboration, in particular the strong support from the Lan Kwai Fong Association and the active participation of various government departments. These include the Architectural Services Department, the Civil Engineering and Development Department, the Drainage Services Department, the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, the Highways Department, and the Planning Department. By utilising their own resources and going the extra mile, the departments have demonstrated an exemplary team spirit to serve the goal of benefiting the public, tourists, and business." Blending innovative projection technology with lighting effects, the light art show will run from 7pm to 2am the next day on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Transforming the stone wall on D'Aguilar Street and the nearby road surface into a stage, the three-minute show, which creates interactive spatial and visual effects, will be played on a loop once every 10 minutes. The inaugural theme will be Halloween, with subsequent themes introduced for different festivals and events, offering visitors a continuous stream of fresh experiences and surprises. In addition, the Lan Kwai Fong Association has commissioned the street art team, "All in One", to create a large-scale mural on the retaining wall adjacent to D'Aguilar Street. The 43-metre-long mural, with a theme of the transformation of Lan Kai Fong from the past to the present, extends from D'Aguilar Street to Wing Wah Lane. It is set to become a new photo spot in the area. A QR code will later be added to the mural. Visitors may use their mobile phones or smart devices to learn more about Lan Kwai Fong, a renowned round-the-clock entertainment hub. The Lan Kwai Fong Association will also host Halloween activities in Lan Kwai Fong on October 24 and 31. Members of the public and tourists can dress up in creative festive costumes and enjoy special art installations, such as the light art show and mural, immersing themselves in the vibrant festive experience of Lan Kwai Fong. The spokesperson said, "This is only the initial step of the upgrading of Lan Kwai Fong to 'version 2.0'. The beautification works of the Lan Kwai Fong Public Refuse Collection Point, located next to the Lan Kwai Fong Sitting-out Area along Lan Kwai Fong trail, is also close to completion to better integrate with the surrounding urban design. We will also be gradually completing repaving works of the remaining roads in the core area of Lan Kwai Fong by mid-2027. Furthermore, the DEVB will commission a 'community-making' consultancy study in the first quarter of 2027 to prepare for the second phase of the beautification works. We look forward to the reinvention of Lan Kwai Fong upon the conclusion of the two phases, drawing in even more visitors." Lan Kwai Fong has been an iconic dining and nightlife landmark in Hong Kong. The Government launched a beautification project in the area in phases with a view to enhancing the environment and attracting visitors. The first phase of the project involves resurfacing the pavement and roads in the core area of Lan Kwai Fong with distinctive patterns, creating a unique atmosphere and offering a different visual experience to the otherwise ordinary streetscape. The second phase covers nearby streets outside the core area of Lan Kwai Fong, including Wellington Street, Lyndhurst Terrace, and Pottinger Street. According to the preliminary plan, the second phase of the project will incorporate more design elements, including enhancing the facilities on Wo On Lane and the Lok Hing Lane Sitting-out Area, which can serve as an open-air theater; improving signages within the area and enhancing synergy with Pottinger Street in attracting visitors. Meanwhile, a large-scale installation has been launched at the junction of Connaught Road Central and Pedder Street in Central with the DEVB offering policy support and facilitating departmental approvals. The owners of the relevant commercial buildings have also funded the widening of a section of the pavement on Pedder Street to increase pedestrian accessibility. Both of these initiatives demonstrate the Government's dedication in the renewal of Central to breathe new life into Hong Kong's first-generation central business district while preserving its heritage as outlined in the 2026 Policy Address.

items.title: Grading of beach water quality released
items.description: The Environmental Protection Department (EPD) today (October 23) released the latest grading of water quality for 39 gazetted beaches (see Note 1) and one non-gazetted beach (see Note 2). Twenty-eight beaches were rated as Good (Grade 1) and 12 as Fair (Grade 2). Grade 1 beaches are: Big Wave Bay Beach* Lo So Shing Beach Cafeteria New Beach* Lower Cheung Sha Beach Cafeteria Old Beach Pui O Beach* Castle Peak Beach Repulse Bay Beach* Cheung Chau Tung Wan Beach* Shek O Beach* Chung Hom Kok Beach Silver Mine Bay Beach* Clear Water Bay First Beach* South Bay Beach* Clear Water Bay Second Beach* St. Stephen's Beach* Discovery Bay Tai Pak Beach Stanley Main Beach* Hap Mun Bay Beach* Tai Po Lung Mei Beach* Hung Shing Yeh Beach* Tong Fuk Beach Kadoorie Beach* Trio Beach* Kiu Tsui Beach Turtle Cove Beach Kwun Yam Beach Upper Cheung Sha Beach Grade 2 beaches are: Anglers' Beach* Hoi Mei Wan Beach* Approach Beach* Lido Beach* Butterfly Beach* Ma Wan Tung Wan Beach* Casam Beach* Middle Bay Beach* Deep Water Bay Beach* Silverstrand Beach* Golden Beach* Ting Kau Beach* Compared with the grading released last week, Big Wave Bay Beach, Castle Peak Beach, Silver Mine Bay Beach and Turtle Cove Beach have been upgraded from Grade 2 to Grade 1. Under the present grading system, beaches are classified into four grades, namely Good (Grade 1), Fair (Grade 2), Poor (Grade 3) and Very Poor (Grade 4), according to the level of E. coli in the water. Grades are calculated on the basis of the geometric mean of the E. coli counts on the five most recent sampling occasions. While the ratings represent the general water quality at the beaches, an EPD spokesman reminded members of the public that water quality could be temporarily affected during and after periods of heavy rain. Bathers should avoid swimming at beaches for up to three days after a tropical cyclone or heavy rainfall. A summary of beach grades is published weekly before the weekend. The latest beach grades based on the most current data may be obtained from the EPD's website on Beach Water Quality ( www.epd.gov.hk/epd/beach ) or the beach hotline, 2511 6666. Members of the public can also obtain the latest daily water quality forecast information for all beaches that are open for swimming through the EPD's dedicated webpage on the beach water quality forecast ( www.epd.gov.hk/en/BWQForecast ). Note 1: Lifesaving services are provided by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department at 29 gazetted beaches, marked with an asterisk (*) above, from September 1. For details, please refer to the Leisure and Cultural Services Department's Special Announcement ( www.lcsd.gov.hk/en/beach/index.html ). Note 2: This refers to Discovery Bay Tai Pak Beach which has no lifesaving service.

items.title: Local premieres of three films "We Are Born Good", "Afterpiece" and "Spare Queens" financed by Film Development Fund
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Film Development Council (HKFDC): The local premieres of three films which have funding support from the Film Development Fund (FDF), namely "We Are Born Good", "Afterpiece" and "Spare Queens", will be held on October 27, November 3 and November 5 respectively, showcasing the creative achievements of emerging Hong Kong filmmakers and the effectiveness of the FDF in nurturing film talent. "We Are Born Good" is a winning film project in the Higher Education Institution Group of the 8th First Feature Film Initiative (FFFI) funded by the Government. Produced by Patricia Cheng and directed by Yeung Leung-chuen, who co-wrote the screenplay with Wong Wai-man (Thomas), the film stars Yeung Wai-lun, Chung Suet-ying, Kearen Pang, Lo Chun-yip, Ng Wing-sze and Amy Yan. The film tells the story of a feud between the main characters after they quarrelled over a take-away mix-up, and finally became each other's lifeline. It was nominated for the Fei Mu Awards and the Youth Jury Awards at the "Hidden Dragon" section of the 10th Pingyao International Film Festival, among others; selected for the Discovery programme at the 51st Toronto International Film Festival, where it held its world premiere; and also screened at various international film festivals including the 22nd Zurich Film Festival and the 46th Hawaii International Film Festival. The film will be theatrically released in Hong Kong on October 29. Another film funded by the Directors' Succession Scheme (DSS) under the FDF, "Afterpiece", is produced by Derek Yee, directed and written by Keane Wong, and stars Stephen Fung, Angela Yuen, Myolie Wu and Chrissie Chau. The film tells the story of a washed up theatre director who, hoping to reclaim his dignity, decides to write, direct and star in a new play but gradually loses himself between stage and reality. After opening the 28th Shanghai International Film Festival, it was subsequently showcased in various overseas film festivals such as the 25th New York Asian Film Festival, the 45th Vancouver International Film Festival, the 10th Pingyao International Film Festival, and a number of film programmes under the Hong Kong Film Gala Presentations in Thailand, Malaysia and Cambodia. The film will be officially released in Hong Kong on November 12. "Spare Queens" is a winning film project in the Professional Group of the 7th FFFI, funded by the Government. Produced by Chan Hing-kai and O Sing-pui, directed by Tommy Tom, who also co-wrote with Lee Po-chi and Ching Lai, the film stars Stephy Tang, Chrissie Chau, Anson Kong, Adam Pak and Yoyo Tse. The film follows two retired female bowlers, former rivals, who reunite years later to team up on the lanes and face a new challenge. The film was screened at the 50th Hong Kong International Film Festival and the 46th Hawaii International Film Festival, and will be officially released in Hong Kong on November 26. The Chairman of the HKFDC, Dr Wilfred Wong, said that the three FDF-funded films are directed by first-time directors. They are unique and different in styles, with each having its special charms. "We Are Born Good" portrays the perseverance of Hong Kong people, and that the outstanding performances by the two main characters are expected to resonate strongly with audiences. "Afterpiece" skilfully intertwines the emotional conflicts in real life and on stage, creating immense tension with narrative twists and turns. "Spare Queens" is an inspiring story that encourages audiences to face adversity with a sporting spirit on the journey to success. For more information about the FFFI and the DSS, please visit the HKFDC's website at www.fdc.gov.hk/en/applications_detail.php?id=2022042210252142851 and www.fdc.gov.hk/en/dss/index.html .

items.title: Incoming passenger convicted and jailed for possession of duty-not-paid cigarettes (with photo)
items.description: ​An incoming female passenger was sentenced to four weeks' imprisonment with a fine of $500 by the Fanling Magistrates' Courts today (October 23) for possessing duty-not-paid cigarettes and failing to declare them to Customs officers, in contravention of Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO). Customs officers intercepted an incoming 36-year-old local female passenger at the Lok Ma Chau Spur Line Control Point on October 14 and seized 381 duty-not-paid cigarettes from her personal belongings, with an estimated market value of about $1,900, and a duty potential of about $1,260. The female passenger was subsequently arrested. Customs welcomes the sentence. The custodial sentence has imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflects the seriousness of the offences. Members of the public should not defy the law. Customs reminds members of the public that under the DCO, cigarettes are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form ( eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: Inspection of aquatic products imported from Japan
items.description: In response to the Japanese Government's plan to discharge nuclear-contaminated water at the Fukushima Nuclear Power Station, the Director of Food and Environmental Hygiene issued a Food Safety Order which prohibits all aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds originating from the 10 metropolis/prefectures, namely Tokyo, Fukushima, Ibaraki, Miyagi, Chiba, Gunma, Tochigi, Niigata, Nagano and Saitama, from being imported into and supplied in Hong Kong. For other Japanese aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds that are not prohibited from being imported into Hong Kong, the Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department is conducting comprehensive radiological tests to verify that the radiation levels of these products do not exceed the guideline levels before they are allowed to be supplied in the market. From noon on October 22 to noon today (October 23), the CFS conducted tests on the radiological levels of 212 food samples imported from Japan, which were of the "aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt" category. No sample was found to have exceeded the safety limit. Details can be found on the CFS's thematic website titled "Control Measures on Foods Imported from Japan" ( www.cfs.gov.hk/english/programme/programme_rafs/programme_rafs_fc_01_30_Nuclear_Event_and_Food_Safety.html ). In parallel, the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) has also tested 50 samples of local catch for radiological levels. All the samples passed the tests. Details can be found on the AFCD's website ( www.afcd.gov.hk/english/fisheries/Radiological_testing/Radiological_Test.html ). The Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) has also enhanced the environmental monitoring of the local waters. No anomaly has been detected so far. For details, please refer to the HKO's website ( www.hko.gov.hk/en/radiation/monitoring/seawater.html ). From August 24, 2023, to noon today, the CFS and the AFCD have conducted tests on the radiological levels of 269 760 samples of food imported from Japan (including 167 933 samples of aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt) and 57 460 samples of local catch respectively. All the samples passed the tests.

items.title: HKMA designates Primary Liquidity Providers and expands scheme
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced today (October 23) the designation of twelve banks as Primary Liquidity Providers (PLPs) for offshore renminbi (RMB) market in Hong Kong (i.e. CNH market) for a two-year term, with effect from October 27, 2026 following the expiry of the current term, and the increase in the total amount of RMB liquidity available in the PLP Scheme. The twelve PLPs are: Agricultural Bank of China Limited Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited Bank of Communications Co., Ltd. BNP Paribas China CITIC Bank International Limited China Construction Bank (Asia) Corporation Limited Citibank, N.A. Deutsche Bank AG Hang Seng Bank, Limited Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited, The Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (Asia) Limited Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) Limited The PLP selection was based on a range of criteria, including the institution's capability in providing CNH funding and making market for CNH instruments, and commitment to using Hong Kong as a global hub for offshore RMB business. As the result of the designations, the total RMB repo facility dedicated to all PLPs will increase from RMB20 billion to RMB22 billion. The expansion of the PLP Scheme will enhance liquidity support to the offshore RMB market and is conducive to strengthening the position of Hong Kong as the offshore RMB business hub. The HKMA regularly reviews the operation of the scheme and the performance of PLPs and consider the need for refinements, including the number of PLPs and the size of the repo facility.

items.title: 10 building plans approved in August
items.description: The Buildings Department approved 10 building plans in August, with five on Hong Kong Island, three in Kowloon and two in the New Territories. Of the approved plans, seven were for apartment and apartment/commercial developments, two were for factory and industrial development, and one was for community services developments. In the same month, consent was given for works to start on eight building projects which, when completed, will provide 70 908 square metres of gross floor area for domestic use involving 1 442 units, and 24 556 sq m of gross floor area for non-domestic use. The department has received notification of commencement of superstructure works for six building projects. The department also issued 21 occupation permits, with seven on Hong Kong Island, five in Kowloon and nine in the New Territories. Of the buildings certified for occupation, the gross floor area for domestic use was 138 920 sq m involving 1 531 units, and 37 040 sq m was for non-domestic use. The declared cost of new buildings completed in August totalled about $7.7 billion. In addition, seven demolition consents were issued. The department received 3 350 reports about unauthorised building works (UBWs) in August and issued 487 removal orders on UBWs. The full version of the Monthly Digest for August can be viewed on the Buildings Department's homepage ( www.bd.gov.hk ).

items.title: Man sentenced to four weeks' imprisonment for illegally importing alternative smoking products
items.description: ​A man was sentenced today (October 23) at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts to four weeks' imprisonment for illegally importing 25 600 alternative smoking products. The Department of Health (DH) welcomed the verdict and reminded members of the public and visitors not to bring alternative smoking products such as e-cigarettes, heated tobacco products or herbal cigarettes into Hong Kong, and not to use any alternative smoking products. The Tobacco and Alcohol Control Office (TACO) of the DH was notified by Hong Kong Customs yesterday (October 22) that 25 600 alternative smoking products had been intercepted in the luggage of the aforesaid man arriving from Japan. TACO immediately arrested and prosecuted the individual. Since the amendments to the Tobacco Control Legislation (Amendment) Ordinance 2025, which conferred arrest powers on TACO inspectors, took effect on September 19, 2025, TACO has prosecuted 33 cases involving the importation of large quantities of alternative smoking products. Thirty-six persons have been convicted and sentenced to prison terms ranging from four weeks to eight months. According to the Import and Export Ordinance (Cap. 60), a person who imports alternative smoking products, including electronic smoking products, heated tobacco products and herbal cigarettes, commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of $500,000 and imprisonment for two years; or liable on conviction on indictment to a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Under the Smoking (Public Health) Ordinance (Cap. 371), no person may promote, manufacture, sell, or possess for commercial purposes alternative smoking products. An offender is liable to a fine of $50,000 and imprisonment for six months. TACO will continue to closely monitor and enforce the law to combat related offences. In addition, the DH also cautions the public that alternative smoking products are addictive and are not effective smoking cessation or harm reduction tools. E-cigarettes may increase the risk of cancer, respiratory diseases, and cardiovascular diseases. Smokers are urged to quit smoking as early as possible for their own health and that of others. For assistance, please call the DH's Integrated Smoking Cessation Hotline on 1833 183, or visit www.livetobaccofree.hk for information on quitting.

items.title: Seven candidates nominated for Labour Advisory Board Election of Employee Representatives
items.description: The election of five employee representatives to the Labour Advisory Board (LAB) for the next two-year term commencing on January 1, 2027, will be held on November 28 (Saturday) at the Mei Foo Community Hall, 1/F, Mei Foo Government Complex, 33 Mei Lai Road, Sham Shui Po. The Labour Department (LD) received seven valid nominations of candidates from employee unions registered under the Trade Unions Ordinance during the nomination period from September 14 to October 6, 2026. The candidates, listed in the order of receipt of nomination forms by the LD, are: * Mr Chau Sze-kit Chairman, Hong Kong Construction Industry Employees General Union * Mr Anson Tang Tsz-on President, Hong Kong Government Lifeguards General Union * Mr Yang Kaiqiang Vice Chairman, Hong Kong Seamen's Union * Ms Lai Na President, Hong Kong Social Welfare Employees Association * Ms Tam Kam-lin Vice Chairman, The Federation of Hong Kong & Kowloon Labour Unions * Mr Lo Wai-kit Vice Chairman, Association of Hong Kong Nursing Staff * Mr Lam Kwan-ho Chairman, Marine Inspectors and Senior Assistant Shipping Masters' Association A total of 804 employee unions registered as electors have appointed authorised representatives to vote in this election. The electors will soon be informed in writing of the candidate list and detailed proceedings on the election day. Authorised representatives may cast votes at the polling station at Mei Foo Community Hall, from 9am to 5pm on the election day of November 28. Candidates may monitor the counting of votes in person on the election day. The Assistant Commissioner for Labour (Development) will act as the Returning Officer. The respective lists of candidates and electors with authorised representatives appointed, as well as the rules and procedures for the election, are available on the homepage of the LD ( www.labour.gov.hk/eng/news/LAB_Election2026.htm ). Enquiries on matters relating to this election can be made at 2852 4022. The LAB is a tripartite consultative body comprising representatives of employees and employers to advise the Commissioner for Labour on labour matters.

items.title: EMSD launches revamped Hong Kong Energy Efficiency Registration Scheme for Buildings and operational guidelines in connection with Enhancement Scheme for District Cooling Systems and Centralised Multi-Building Cooling Systems
items.description: The Electrical and Mechanical Services Department (EMSD) launched today (October 23) the revamped Hong Kong Energy Efficiency Registration Scheme for Buildings (HKEERSB) and five new/revised operational guidelines in connection with the Enhancement Scheme for District Cooling Systems and Centralised Multi-Building Cooling Systems. The Government-led Kai Tak District Cooling System (DCS) has demonstrated the viability of developing DCSs in Hong Kong. The Chief Executive announced in the 2025 Policy Address that an enhancement scheme will be rolled out to encourage and facilitate the commissioning of small-scale DCSs or centralised multi-building cooling systems (CMCSs) by non-governmental entities from aspects such as technology, taxation and floor area arrangements, with a view to enhancing the popularity of the relevant technologies and promoting the development of green technology to combat climate change and accelerate Hong Kong to move towards the target of carbon neutrality under the Climate Action Plan 2050. The revamped HKEERSB has expanded the coverage to accept registration applications for DCSs and CMCSs, without the need to separately obtain relevant green certifications. Capital expenditure for such eligible energy-efficient building installations is eligible for a whole deduction when it was incurred for the purpose of profit tax calculation. The operational guidelines introduce best practices, design references and emerging technologies to the trade and users for enhancing the reliability, safety and energy efficiency performance of DCS and CMCS projects. Three guidelines have been revised and two guidelines are newly added: Updated "District Cooling Services Supply Conditions"; Updated "Technical Guidelines for Connection to District Cooling System"; Updated "Guidelines for Excavation Works near the District Cooling System"; Newly added "Guidance Notes on Adoption of MiMEP in DCS"; and Newly added "Guidance Notes on Facility Upkeep of DCS Pipe Network". The revamped HKEERSB and the five operational guidelines will take effect on November 1, 2026, and are available at the EMSD's webpage: HKEERSB www.emsd.gov.hk/en/energy_efficiency/energy_efficiency_registration_scheme_for_building/index.html District Cooling Systems in Hong Kong - Guidelines and Forms www.emsd.gov.hk/en/energy_efficiency/DCS_in_HK/guidelines_forms/index.html Other measures of the Enhancement Scheme will be rolled out in stages, and the scheme will be fully implemented in the first quarter of 2027.

items.title: RTHK signs Memorandum of Understanding with Chengdu Radio and Television (with photos)
items.description: The Director of Broadcasting, Ms Angelina Kwan, led a delegation from Radio Television Hong Kong (RTHK) to visit Chengdu from October 21 to 23. During the visit, RTHK signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Chengdu Radio and Television to prepare to jointly organise the "RTHK Vinyl Pop Up" and other events in Chengdu next year. The collaboration aims to strengthen people-to-people bonds and cultural connections between the two cities, jointly amplify their communication influence, and showcase the cultural soft power of Hong Kong and Chengdu to audiences around the world. Ms Kwan and the President of Chengdu Radio and Television and Chairman of Chengdu Broadcasting (Group) Corporation, Mr Yang Xiaoyang, signed the MOU yesterday (October 22). The two broadcasters will expand co-operation across a range of areas, including programme content exchanges, talent development and related exchanges, collaboration on new media platforms and the organisation of events. A key initiative will be the introduction of RTHK's acclaimed signature project, the "RTHK Vinyl Pop Up", to Chengdu in the second quarter of next year. The event has previously been staged in Hong Kong, Qianhai in Shenzhen, and Shanghai. During the visit, the RTHK delegation also met with senior management of the Chengdu Media Group to exchange views and explore further opportunities for collaboration. Ms Kwan said that RTHK has long been committed to strengthening ties with media organisations across the Chinese Mainland through broadcasting and cultural exchanges, thereby fostering people-to-people bonds between Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland. RTHK expressed hopes that bringing the "RTHK Vinyl Pop Up" to Chengdu would allow music to serve as a bridge for introducing Hong Kong's pop culture to a wider Mainland audience, while helping to share the stories of both Hong Kong and Chengdu with the world.

items.title: Health Bureau announces commencement of patient pairing arrangements under Community Pharmacy Programme (Community) and annual consultation co-payment adjustments of Primary Healthcare Co-care Network
items.description: The Health Bureau (HHB) announced today (October 23) that the Community Pharmacy Programme (CPP) (Community) will launch the patient pairing arrangement with designated community pharmacies by the end of October. In addition, the annually adjusted consultation co-payment fees for the screening and treatment phases, as allowed to be set by family doctors participating in the Primary Healthcare Co-care Network (Co-care Network) according to the established mechanism, will take effect from November 1. CPP (Community)'s patient pairing arrangements To implement the Primary Healthcare Blueprint's recommendations of adopting a multidisciplinary approach for the proper management of chronic diseases in the community, strengthen the professional role of community pharmacists, and provide patients with more options for drug dispensing or refill services, as well as medication counselling and management services in the community, the first phase of the CPP (Community) will be piloted at four districts to launch patient pairing arrangements for designated family doctors participating in the Co-care Network and Family Medicine Clinics of the Hospital Authority (HA), with a total of 20 designated pharmacies across the districts. Upon successful pairing, participating patients will be able to obtain drugs from their preferred pharmacy, with pharmacists providing medication counselling and related drug and health advice, thereby enhancing patients' drug compliance and personal health management. Drug refill services at community pharmacies can also help prevent the accumulation of excess drugs at home by patients, reducing the risk of improper storage and misuse while minimising potential drug wastage. The first phase of the programme will be piloted at four districts, namely Eastern, Yau Tsim Mong, Sha Tin and Yuen Long, with five community pharmacies conveniently located near residential areas and shopping malls selected in each district (list set out in Annex). The HHB will invite, in phases, family doctors participating in the Co-care Network to join the programme, and will invite eligible patients to enrol and be paired with a designated community pharmacy of their choice, and brief them on details of the drug dispensing or refill arrangements. In future, the second phase of the programme will cover Southern, Wong Tai Sin, Kwun Tong, Tuen Mun, North and Tai Po districts, while the third phase will cover the remaining eight districts. The HHB will extend services to all 18 districts across the city in the fourth quarter of next year. More eligible pharmacies in each district will also be invited to join the programme thereafter. For those using community pharmacies under the programme, drug co-payment for Co-care Network participants will be charged in accordance with the arrangements of the Community Drug Formulary, while drug fees for HA patients will remain aligned with the HA's prevailing fee schedule. More details on the Community Drug Formulary and the operation of the CPP (Community) will be announced in due course. Co-care Network's annual consultation co-payment adjustments Under the co-payment model of the Co-care Network, the Government provides a partial subsidy, while participants are required to pay a certain amount of co-payment fee, with a view to encouraging citizens to bear the primary responsibility for their own health. Participating family doctors are allowed to determine the consultation co-payment fees for the screening phase (not more than $120 for cardiovascular disease risk factor screening and not more than $180 for chronic hepatitis B screening) and the treatment phase on their own, and have the fees adjusted once annually according to the established mechanism. The list of consultation co-payment fees for the screening and treatment phases taking effect from November 1 has been uploaded to the dedicated website of the Co-care Network for public reference. Relevant information on the webpage for searching family doctors will also be updated on the same day. Regarding the treatment phase, following the co-payment fee adjustment, the proportion of service points charging consultation co-payment fees at or below the Government-recommended level of $150 will remain above 60 per cent (773 service points), while the median co-payment remains at $150. Among the current 1 239 participating service points, 1 022 of them (i.e. 82.5 per cent) will keep their existing co-payment fees unchanged. Twenty-eight service points will reduce their co-payment fees (the median reduction is $100), while the remaining 189 service points will increase their co-payment fees, of which nearly 90 per cent will raise their fees by $50 or below. Overall, the rate of increase of the consultation co-payment fees for the treatment phase is 3.7 per cent in the coming year. For the co-payment fees for the screening phase, the vast majority of service points (over 97 per cent) will charge the Government-recommended co-payment levels. In addition, 28 and 20 service points will charge co-payments below the Government-recommended level for cardiovascular disease risk factor screening and chronic hepatitis B screening respectively. As at October 7 (Note 1) this year, more than 300 000 citizens have enrolled in the Co-care Network. Among the participants who have completed cardiovascular disease risk factor screening and/or chronic hepatitis B screening, around 70 000 have been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease risk factors (i.e. suffering from diabetes mellitus, hypertension or hyperlipidaemia, or prediabetes (Note 2)) and/or chronic hepatitis B, and have entered the treatment phase. For more details of the CPP, members of the public may visit its dedicated website or call the hotline at 2525 2328. For more details of the Co-care Network, members of the public may visit its dedicated website or call the hotline at 2157 0500. Dedicated staff of both hotlines will answer calls from 9am to 9pm from Monday to Saturday. Note 1: These are provisional figures, subject to revision upon the availability of updated data. Note 2: Prediabetes refers to HbA1c levels of 6.0-6.4 per cent or FPG levels of 6.1-6.9 mmol/L.

items.title: HKSAR LegCo strongly condemns and resolutely opposes UK's six-monthly report on Hong Kong
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Legislative Council Secretariat: A spokesperson for the Legislative Council (LegCo) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) today (October 23) expressed resolute opposition and issued a strong condemnation regarding the untruthful allegations, slanders and smears targeting various aspects of the HKSAR in the so-called six-monthly report on Hong Kong (January to June 2026) published by the United Kingdom (UK) Government. LegCo firmly supports the solemn statement issued by the HKSAR Government to refute the UK's disregard for facts. The HKSAR is an inalienable part of the People's Republic of China. The core essence of the Sino-British Joint Declaration is China's resumption of the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong. It is not an "international treaty" that confers upon the UK any continuous right of supervision over the HKSAR after its return to the motherland. With China's resumption of the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong in 1997, all rights and obligations concerning the UK under the Joint Declaration have been completely fulfilled. Following Hong Kong's return, the constitutional and legal basis for the Chinese Government to govern Hong Kong is the Constitution of the People's Republic of China and the Basic Law of the HKSAR of the People's Republic of China. The UK has no sovereignty, jurisdiction or right of supervision over the HKSAR, and has no right whatsoever to interfere in the affairs of the Region. The LegCo spokesperson reiterated that the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL) and the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance are institutional foundations for Hong Kong to restore order, safeguard freedom and development. The UK report portrays Hong Kong's improvement of national security legislation and law enforcement as an erosion of rights and freedoms, while deliberately evading a fundamental fact: prior to the implementation of the HKNSL, Hong Kong experienced severe violent turmoil, public order was severely impacted, and the personal safety and normal lives of citizens were directly threatened. Following the implementation of the HKNSL, Hong Kong society has restored peace and order, providing a solid foundation for developments in Hong Kong's economy, people's livelihood and other aspects. The UK ignores the actual situation of Hong Kong society returning to stability and safety, and its so-called report is purely a pretext to stir up trouble. In fact, the UK itself possesses at least 14 pieces of legislation safeguarding national security. A country that relies on such an intensive system of national security laws to safeguard its own security stigmatises the law enforcement and judicial measures taken by Hong Kong against a tiny minority of acts endangering national security as undermining rights and freedoms. Such hypocritical double standards precisely expose the political manipulation essence of the report, rather than a genuine concern for the rule of law and human rights. The LegCo spokesperson emphasised that Hong Kong's judicial independence is fully protected by the Basic Law. Courts independently adjudicate cases strictly based on evidence and the law, and all reasons for verdicts and sentencing judgments are fully public and free from political interference. The World Justice Project recently released the Rule of Law Index 2026, showing that Hong Kong's ranking remains high and unchanged, maintaining sixth place in East Asia and the Pacific region and ranking 24th among 143 countries and regions globally. Hong Kong's scores in most areas remain comparable to last year, with rankings continuing to lead individual Western countries that unceasingly and unreasonably criticise Hong Kong's rule of law and human rights situation. The LegCo spokesperson reiterated that Hong Kong is a society underpinned by the rule of law, where laws must be obeyed and lawbreakers held accountable. Courts in Hong Kong strictly follow the law to adjudicate cases concerning offences endangering national security, including the "Lai Chee-ying case", in a fair and impartial manner, and openly explain the reasons for verdicts and sentencing; conviction decisions are all reasoned and well-founded. The UK Government's so-called report groundlessly attacks Hong Kong's judicial system and trials, and even unreasonably demands the release of convicted persons, which is overtly placing politics above court judgments. This is a blatant trampling on the rule of law and a gross interference in Hong Kong's judicial independence. Hong Kong has entered a new stage of advancing from stability to prosperity, where security and legal systems are effectively safeguarded, governance efficacy is enhanced, social order is stable, the business environment is continuously optimised, and residents' rights and freedoms are fully protected in accordance with the law. If the UK is genuinely concerned about Hong Kong, it should face these facts and establish a pragmatic and constructive relationship with Hong Kong. The LegCo spokesperson strongly urged the UK Government to stop publishing untruthful and highly misleading so-called reports regarding Hong Kong affairs, and to stop interfering in the HKSAR affairs which are purely China's internal affairs. The spokesperson reiterated that LegCo will, as always, under the executive-led system, firmly support the HKSAR Government in administering in accordance with the law, ensuring the steadfast and successful implementation of "one country, two systems".

items.title: Speech by SFST at Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK Festival 2026 press conference (English only)
items.description: Following is the speech by the Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Mr Christopher Hui, at the press conference on Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK Festival 2026 today (October 23): Alpha (Director-General of Investment Promotion, Ms Alpha Lau), ladies and gentlemen, Good morning and thank you for joining us today. In about a week's time, Hong Kong will once again welcome innovators, entrepreneurs, investors, corporates and policymakers from around the world for Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK Festival 2026. I have had the privilege of witnessing this premier gathering transform into a global powerhouse for innovation over the years. Entering its 11th edition this year, the event reaches another milestone. We are delighted to welcome over 45 000 executives, more than 1 000 renowned speakers, and 800 sponsors and exhibitors from over 120 economies to join us. This is of particular significance when we just had the APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) Finance Ministers' Meeting completed in Hong Kong earlier this week, and one of the key discussion areas at the meeting exactly falls on digital infrastructure financing. In tandem with Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address, which set out the blueprint for our city's future development, this year's Hong Kong FinTech Week carries the forward looking theme "Fintech Nexus: Bridging the World, Building the Future". Our position at the forefront of global fintech is not merely rhetorical, but a proven reality on the world stage. As one of the top international financial centres globally and a leading force in Asia, Hong Kong continues to make confident strides in expanding its fintech capability. Today, Hong Kong continues to be one of the most prestigious centres on development of fintech. We are proud to host a thriving community of more than 1 400 fintech companies, including eight digital banks, four virtual insurers, and 12 licensed virtual asset trading platforms. Our success does not happen by accident. It stems from sustained policy vision, strong regulatory direction, and a firm commitment to implementation. Let me highlight the major milestones we have achieved over the past year across a few key focus areas. First of all in tokenisation, Hong Kong is moving beyond experimentation and into implementation. Earlier this year, we have concluded the first phase of a joint review with the HKMA (Hong Kong Monetary Authority) on the adoption of distributed ledger technology (DLT) in Hong Kong's fixed income market, confirming that Hong Kong's legal and regulatory framework is already sufficiently flexible to support tokenised bond issuances. To provide the market with certainty about DLT record-keeping, we have issued a clarification affirming that a register of debenture holders maintained with the use of DLT can be deemed as fulfilling the relevant record-keeping requirements under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). Market adoption is growing rapidly. By the end of last year, banks in Hong Kong held more than $14 billion in digital assets under custody, while tokenised deposits reached $29 billion. Just last month, the Government completed its fourth digital green bond issuance, raising approximately $20 billion equivalent and setting another global record for the largest digital bond issuance in the world. The offering was oversubscribed across four currencies, demonstrating strong investor demand and growing market adoption of tokenised financial products. It also marked the world's first digital bond integrating tokenised Hong Kong dollar (HKD) deposits into the settlement process, highlighting how Hong Kong continues to lead the development of next-generation financial infrastructure. Building on this impressive momentum in tokenised finance, we are making steady progress under our digital assets policy. Under the direction of the Policy Statement 2.0 (Policy Statement 2.0 on the Development of Digital Assets in Hong Kong), we have been broadening the range of tokenised products, expanding practical use cases and strengthening collaboration across the financial ecosystem. In particular, the HKMA granted stablecoin issuer licences to two entities in April this year, with one licensed issuer beginning to issue its regulated HKD-pegged stablecoin in August 2026 and the other expected to do the same very soon. In parallel with digital asset innovation, we are scaling artificial intelligence and data infrastructure across our financial sectors. Through the Generative AI Sandbox++ launched by the HKMA, the SFC (Securities and Futures Commission), the Insurance Authority, and the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority alongside Cyberport, we expanded the sandbox initiative to multiple financial sectors, including banking, securities and capital markets, asset and wealth management, insurance, mandatory provident fund, and also stored value facilities. To complement these technological capabilities, we are continuing to broaden the reach of our financial data infrastructure. We are actively encouraging more government departments and institutions to integrate with the Commercial Data Interchange (CDI) and explore the feasibility of automated payment. This will enable banks to conduct a business registration search through CDI, enhancing efficiency in credit approval. Digital finance is also integrated in our new financial development of the commodity market. As a key infrastructure to develop Hong Kong into a trusted international gold trading, clearing, and reserve hub, the Government has commenced the trial operation of the central clearing and settlement system for over-the-counter gold transactions. In this system, we have established a central digital ledger to record settlement activities and interface seamlessly with designated vaults to facilitate and record physical gold deposits and withdrawals. Before we officially launch this system in Q1 next year as stated in the Policy Address, we will also have the system connected to the Real Time Gross Settlement system to enable Delivery versus Payment settlement. Moreover, an HAU price ticker was launched to reflect indicative bid/offer prices contributed by gold market participants and is now providing reference data on Bloomberg and London Stock Exchange Group platforms. Our regulators are also forerunners in fintech development. As stated in the 2026 Policy Address, the SFC will improve its regulatory framework to facilitate the issuance and trading of tokenised products of gold and other suitable real-world assets on licensed platforms. The HKEX (Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited) is striving to launch a pilot project for tokenised warehouse-receipt financing with designated banks next year, using physical tracking technologies to promote the use of commodity inventories as collateral. The HKEX is also developing a blockchain-backed, multi-asset tokenisation platform which will include commodity warehouse receipts from LME (London Metal Exchange)-approved warehouses for a pilot next year. All these are leveraging our strength in fintech to support our building of a more integrated gold ecosystem and injecting new momentum into the development of the financial sector. Looking ahead, we are doubling down on this momentum with a clear, forward focused strategy. We will continue to leverage our strengths in Finance+ and AI+ to consolidate our status as an international financial centre, driving fintech development to capitalise on new growth opportunities. This is not just about maintaining our lead. It is also about shaping the next chapter of global finance, where capital flows more intelligently and technology addresses real world economic challenges. So I invite each of you, every one of you here today, to join us at the Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK Festival. Let us explore the boundless possibilities of fintech in Hong Kong. Let us pave the way for a connected, efficient, and sustainable global economy. Thank you.

items.title: Hong Kong Customs seizes live turtles of suspected scheduled endangered species (with photo)
items.description: ​Hong Kong Customs yesterday (October 22) seized two live turtles of suspected scheduled endangered species, with an estimated market value of about $3,000, at the Lok Ma Chau Spur Line Control Point. Customs officers intercepted an incoming 50-year-old local male passenger at the Arrival Hall of the above-mentioned control point yesterday. Upon examination, the two live turtles were seized from his plastic bag. Officers of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) attended the scene for inspection and preliminarily identified the two live turtles as of endangered species listed in the Appendices to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora and regulated under the Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance in Hong Kong. The case was handed over to the AFCD for follow-up investigation. Customs reminds the public not to carry controlled items into and out of Hong Kong. Under the Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance (Cap. 586), any person importing, exporting or possessing specimens of endangered species not in accordance with the Ordinance commits an offence and will be liable to a maximum fine of $10 million and imprisonment for 10 years upon conviction with the specimens forfeited. Members of the public may report any suspected smuggling activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form (​ eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: Legendary Brazilian guitar duo Assad Brothers to bring farewell tour to Hong Kong on October 30 (with photos)
items.description: The fourth Asia+ Festival will present the concert "Guitar Duo Recital by Assad Brothers" on October 30. Being leading figures in the classical guitar world for over half a century, this Hong Kong performance is part of the Brazilian Assad Brothers' farewell tour of their 60-year musical partnership. Local guzheng virtuoso Wan Xing will join the duo, offering a musical exchange that transcends geographical and cultural boundaries. The Assad brothers, Sérgio and Odair, have been acclaimed for their virtuosity and telepathic unity. Their music fuses Brazilian folk, Latin, jazz, and classical elements, earning them multiple Latin Grammy Awards over the years. The concert will bring together much-loved works from the duo's repertoire, including mesmerising tango music by Argentine composer Astor Piazzolla, Brazilian-flavoured works by Brazilian composer Heitor Villa-Lobos, and original compositions by Sérgio Assad, alongside Brazilian musical treasures rarely heard in Hong Kong. To mark the China-Brazil Year of Culture, Wan will also share the stage for a piece inspired by the folkloric legend of Mulan, in which the oriental resonance of guzheng intertwines with the Latin flair of guitar, crafting an exquisite melody that bridges East and West. The concert "Guitar Duo Recital by Assad Brothers" will be held at 8pm on October 30 at the Hong Kong City Hall Concert Hall. Tickets priced at $200, $300 and $420 are available at URBTIX ( www.urbtix.hk ). For telephone bookings, please call 3166 1288 or use the mobile ticketing app URBTIX. Fringe activities including a pre-concert talk and guitar masterclasses are also available. For details, please refer to www.asiaplus.gov.hk/2026/en/assad-brothers . Presented by the Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau and organised by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department, the Asia+ Festival is held annually from September to November. Themed "Traditions Recast", this year's festival brings together over 30 countries and regions, and presents more than 100 performances and related activities, showcasing the artistic essence of Asia and countries and regions along the Belt and Road. For programme enquiries and ticketing concessions, please call 2370 1044 or visit www.asiaplus.gov.hk .

items.title: Appointment of Chairman of Market Misconduct Tribunal and Securities and Futures Appeals Tribunal announced
items.description: The Government announced today (October 23) that the Chief Executive has appointed Mr Mohan Tarachand Bharwaney, a former Judge of the Court of First Instance of the High Court, as a Chairman of the Market Misconduct Tribunal (MMT) and the Securities and Futures Appeals Tribunal (SFAT) for a term of three years, starting from December 1, 2026, and January 1, 2027, respectively. A Government spokesman said, "Mr Bharwaney has over 40 years of experience in the legal profession. He joined the Judiciary in 2010 and retired from the Court of First Instance of the High Court in 2021. We are confident that with his sterling experience and knowledge in adjudication and legal matters, Mr Bharwaney will lead the Tribunals to operate effectively." The Government also expressed gratitude to the outgoing Chairman of the Tribunals, Mr Michael John Hartmann, for his valuable contributions and dedicated service. As authorised by the Chief Executive, Mr Hartmann will complete any cases that he has commenced before the expiry of his term of appointment. Both the MMT and the SFAT are established under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) (SFO). The MMT deals with six types of market misconduct, namely insider dealing, false trading, price rigging, disclosure of information about prohibited transactions, disclosure of false or misleading information inducing transactions, and stock market manipulation. The MMT is also empowered to deal with the breaches of disclosure requirements on price sensitive information of listed corporations. The SFAT has jurisdiction to review specified decisions made under the SFO by the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and an investor compensation company recognised by the SFC. It serves as an effective safeguard to ensure that the relevant regulatory decisions are reasonable and fair. Mr Michael Victor Lunn, a former Vice-President of the Court of Appeal of the High Court, and Mr Ian Charles McWalters, a former Justice of Appeal of the Court of Appeal of the High Court, are the other serving Chairmen of the MMT and the SFAT.

items.title: Employer sanctioned for violating requirements of local recruitment under Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme
items.description: The Labour Department (LD) today (October 23) announced the imposition of an administrative sanction on Hong Kong-Shenzhen Vehicle Services Limited. With immediate effect, the LD has terminated the processing of an application for importing labour previously submitted by the company under the Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme (ESLS). In parallel, the LD will, from today, refuse to process any applications submitted by the company under the ESLS for a period of two years. A spokesman for the LD said, "After an investigation, it was established that the above company had breached the local recruitment requirements under the ESLS while seeking to import a driver. An administrative sanction is thus imposed for the following reasons: (i) failing to interview a qualified job seeker as scheduled without a reasonable excuse; and (ii) providing the LD with false information on the interview results." The spokesman stressed, "Employers applying for the importation of workers under the ESLS should strictly comply with the scheme requirements, including according priority to employing suitable local workers. The ESLS stipulates that if an employer violates labour or immigration laws, the requirements of the ESLS, or the Standard Employment Contract, the LD will impose an administrative sanction on the employer. Such sanctions may include terminating the processing of submitted applications of the employer, withdrawing approvals for the importation of workers previously granted, and refusing to process any subsequent applications submitted by the employer."
