items.title: Government announces appointments of Panel Judges under Interception of Communications and Surveillance Ordinance
items.description: The Government announced today (October 23) that the Chief Executive, on the recommendation of the Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal, has appointed two Judges of the Court of First Instance of the High Court as Panel Judges under the Interception of Communications and Surveillance Ordinance (Chapter 589). The Chief Executive has reappointed Mr Justice Poon Siu-tung as a Panel Judge under the Ordinance for a term of three years from October 25, 2026, to October 24, 2029. He has also appointed Mr Justice Leung Chun-man as a Panel Judge under the Ordinance for a term of three years from October 25, 2026, to October 24, 2029. Mr Justice Leung Chun-man was called to the Bar in Hong Kong in 1991. He was in private practice from 1992 until he joined the Judiciary as a District Judge in 2007. He was appointed as a Judge of the Court of First Instance of the High Court in 2024. The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, said, "Mr Justice Poon Siu-tung has demonstrated full dedication in handling the law enforcement agencies' applications for authorisations under the Ordinance during the past term. I am confident that Mr Justice Poon Siu-tung and the newly appointed Panel Judge Mr Justice Leung Chun-man will make use of their expertise and experience to ensure the effective operation of the regulatory regime under the Ordinance." The Ordinance provides a comprehensive statutory framework for regulating the conduct of interception and covert surveillance by law enforcement agencies, and aims to strike a balance between maintaining law and order and protecting the privacy rights of individuals. Under the Ordinance, Panel Judges shall consider applications for authorisations of interception and Type 1 surveillance and for device retrieval warrants.

items.title: Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Pearl River Delta Regional Air Quality Monitoring Network results for 2025 released
items.description: Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao jointly released today (October 23) a report on air quality in 2025 under the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Pearl River Delta Regional Air Quality Monitoring Network, which indicates a long-term downward trend of the concentrations of various air pollutants, namely sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, respirable suspended particulates and fine suspended particulates. Compared with 20 years ago, the 2025 annual average concentrations for these parameters have declined by between 23 per cent and 86 per cent (shown in Annexes 1 and 2). Among these, fine suspended particulates concentration dropped to 19 μg/m³, reaching a leading level nationwide. This reflects the effectiveness of the emission reduction measures implemented by the three places in improving air quality across the Pearl River Delta region. Over the past few years, the governments of Guangdong, Hong Kong, and Macao have introduced various policy measures and co-operated to improve regional air quality. For Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government has continued to implement various air pollutant emission control measures covered in the Hong Kong Roadmap on Popularisation of Electric Vehicles (EVs), the Clean Air Plan for Hong Kong 2035, the Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan 2050 and the Green Transformation Roadmap of Public Buses and Taxis on marine and land transport, power plants and non-road mobile machinery to enhance air quality. Also, the Updated Version of the Hong Kong Roadmap on Popularisation of EVs, announced in February 2026, updates the strategies and measures for promoting the popularisation of EVs. In addition, the Air Pollution Control (Amendment) Ordinance 2025 came into effect in April, 2025, updating a number of air quality objectives (AQOs). Among the 15 updated AQOs, seven are set at the most stringent levels of the World Health Organization Global Air Quality Guidelines, which are on par with those of other advanced economies. On the reduction of emissions from power plants, the HKSAR Government published the Tenth Technical Memorandum for Allocation of Emission Allowances In Respect of Specified Licences (TM) in May 2025 to further tighten the emission caps of air pollutants for electricity sector from 2030 onwards. Compared with the First TM (i.e. emission allowance for 2010), the emission allowances for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and respirable suspended particulates have been reduced by about 91 per cent, 80 per cent and 75 per cent respectively. The HKSAR Government has also amended the Air Pollution Control (Fuel Restriction) Regulations in 2025, and is planning to amend the Air Pollution Control (Marine Light Diesel) Regulation. These amendments tighten the sulphur content limit of local industrial and commercial liquid fuel and marine light diesel to 0.001 per cent, on par with vehicle diesel standards, achieving "three-oil integration" in Hong Kong. Besides, the HKSAR Government continues to commit to phasing out approximately 40 000 Euro IV diesel commercial vehicles progressively by the end of 2027. As at end-August 2026, more than 33 700 target vehicles had been phased out, and roadside remote sensing equipment is deployed to monitor vehicle exhaust emissions. Hong Kong will cease new registrations of fuel-propelled private cars including hybrids in 2035 or earlier, and will introduce 700 electric buses and 3 000 electric taxis by the end of 2027 to actively promote the green transformation of vehicles, aiming to achieve zero vehicular emissions before 2050. As at end-September 2026, there are about 185 600 EVs in Hong Kong, including about 180 300 electric private cars, which is approximately six times the figure in 2021 and accounts for about 27.6 per cent of all private cars in Hong Kong. The number of parking spaces with charging facilities in Hong Kong exceeded 170 000, including around 18 090 public chargers. The overall charging infrastructure is sufficient to support more than 290 000 EVs. Regarding marine vessels, Hong Kong and cities in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) have collaborated since 2019 to establish a domestic marine emission control area in the Pearl River Delta, requiring all vessels to use compliant fuel within Hong Kong waters while sailing or at berth. Since the implementation of the above measures, the annual average concentration of sulphur dioxide recorded in 2025 at the Kwai Chung Air Quality Monitoring Station in the vicinity of the Kwai Chung Container Terminals has reduced by about 50 per cent as compared with 2018, indicating that the control measures have been effective. The HKSAR Government has also been encouraging local ferries to adopt green transportation technologies to reduce air pollutant emissions. This includes the implementation of the Pilot Scheme for Electric Ferries. The three electric ferries that have commenced trials are operating smoothly overall, providing passengers with a diesel-odour-free, quiet and comfortable experience when crossing Victoria Harbour. Meanwhile, Guangdong Province published and implemented the "Notice on Action Plan for Continuous Improvement of Air Quality in Guangdong Province Issued by the People's Government of Guangdong Province", the "Notice on Implementation of Monitoring Requirements on Fugitive Emission of Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) from Factories Issued by Department of Ecology and Environment of Guangdong Province", the "Notice on Strengthening Control of VOCs Emissions During Storage and Transportation in Oil Depots and Petrochemical and Chemical Enterprises", the "Notice on Further Reduction of Nitrogen Oxides Emission from Stationary and Mobile Sources issued by Department of Ecology and Environment of Guangdong Province", and the "Notice on Strengthening Environmental Control on Diesel Trucks of Key Vehicle-using Enterprises", as well as promulgating the local standard "Integrated Emission Standard of VOCs for Stationary Pollution Source". Guangdong Province launched the hierarchical management of VOCs-related enterprises, enhanced the total VOCs management, advanced the control of industrial boilers and furnaces, upheld a co-ordinated approach across vehicle regulations, fuel standards, roadway management, and enterprise compliance to strengthen emissions regulations for diesel trucks operated by key enterprises, conducted compliance checks on new vehicles, improved emissions management for non-road mobile machinery, and carried out regular sampling and inspection of the fuel quality and emissions of engineering machinery. The Macao Special Administrative Region Government (Macao SAR Government) is continuously implementing measures to improve air quality in line with policies such as the Long-term Decarbonisation Strategy of Macao (including the Electric Vehicle Promotion Plan of Macao) and the Environmental Protection Planning of Macao, which include phasing out high-pollution vehicles, promoting EVs, and controlling vehicle exhaust emissions. The previously launched Subsidy Scheme for Phasing out Old Motorcycles with Replacement of New Electric Motorcycles and the Subsidy Scheme for Phasing Out Old Diesel Vehicles have effectively driven the elimination of highly polluting old motorcycles and diesel vehicles. In addition to this, the Government is launching a five-year Plan for Granting Financial Support for the Scrapping of Gasoline-powered Motorcycles and their Replacement by New Electric Motorcycles in 2025, and the third phase of the Subsidy Scheme for Phasing Out Old Diesel Vehicles in 2026. This new phase expands the scope of eligible applicants, further intensifying efforts to phase out high-polluting vehicles and promote electric motorcycles. Meanwhile, to effectively align with and implement the Nation's 15th Five-Year Plan and the Macao SAR's 3rd Five-Year Plan, and to contribute to achieving the national "Dual Carbon Goals", the Macao SAR Government has proactively advanced a series of EV promotion policies. These include lowering EV charging fees again in 2026, constructing supercharging stations for light and heavy vehicles, carefully analysing the charging characteristics of different public car parks and parking spots to adjust the ratio of EV fast and slow chargers, and enhancing public charging and battery-swapping facilities to increase incentives and convenience for using EVs. In addition, the Macao SAR Government has continuously reviewed vehicle tailpipe emission standards, tightening the limits for certain parameters of motor vehicle unleaded petrol in 2025, and will further tighten the emission limits for in-use motorcycles and diesel vehicles by the end of 2026. Furthermore, the Government continues to explore the potential of photovoltaic applications in public spaces and to optimise the proportion of clean electricity in the energy structure, thereby further controlling local atmospheric pollutant emissions and improving air quality. The Network comprises a total of 23 air monitoring stations in Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao. The Ecological and Environmental Monitoring Centre of Guangdong, the Environmental Protection Department (EPD) of Hong Kong, the Macao Environmental Protection Bureau and the Macao Meteorological and Geophysical Bureau are responsible for the co-ordination, management and operation of the monitoring stations in the respective places and the release of quarterly and annual monitoring results. The relevant reports are available on the following websites: The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Regional Air Quality Monitoring Information System ( www.gdeem.cn:20047/#/ ); The Department of Ecology and Environment of Guangdong Province ( gdee.gd.gov.cn ); The EPD of Hong Kong ( www.epd.gov.hk ); and The Macao Environmental Protection Bureau ( www.dspa.gov.mo ) or the Macao Meteorological and Geophysical Bureau ( www.smg.gov.mo ). Looking ahead, the governments of Guangdong, Hong Kong, and Macao will continue to work hand in hand to build a beautiful bay area and further improve air quality in the GBA.

items.title: Chinalco sets up corporate treasury centre in Hong Kong as group's offshore fund management platform (with photo)
items.description: ​ Invest Hong Kong (InvestHK) announced today (October 23) that Aluminum Corporation of China (Chinalco) has set up a corporate treasury centre in Hong Kong, Chinalco Treasury Management Co., Limited (Chinalco Treasury). As the group's offshore fund management platform, Chinalco Treasury will centrally manage the group's offshore funds and handle offshore financing, exchange rate and interest rate risk management, as well as integrated financial services. The move will help this global leader in the non-ferrous metals industry expand overseas, while demonstrating Hong Kong's strengths as the first port of call for Mainland enterprises going global and as a hub for corporate treasury centres. The Director-General of Investment Promotion, Ms Alpha Lau, said, "We warmly welcome Chinalco Teasury setting up in Hong Kong. As the world's largest offshore Renminbi hub, Hong Kong can provide enterprises with cross-border Renminbi settlement, multi-currency fund management and risk hedging capabilities, while actively promoting the wider use of Renminbi in financing and commodity pricing. Coupled with the city's simple tax regime and free flow of capital, InvestHK hopes that Chinalco will use its treasury centre as a starting point to further establish commodity trading functions in Hong Kong, combining the city's pricing, clearing, financing, and warehousing networks with its own industrial strengths to create mutual synergies." Ms Lau added, "This year, the HKSAR (Hong Kong Special Administrative Region) Government unveiled the Action Plan to Promote Development of Corporate Treasury Centres in Hong Kong. Its measures include revamping the tax regime and expanding Hong Kong's network of Comprehensive Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreements, which will make the city more competitive as a hub for corporate treasury centres. InvestHK will continue to provide comprehensive support to enterprises at every stage of going global and empower more Mainland enterprises to expand worldwide through Hong Kong." The Chief Financial Officer of Chinalco, Ms Wang Xin, said, "As the group's overseas industrial presence continues to grow, we need an efficient platform to co-ordinate our offshore funds management. Hong Kong's foreign exchange market is the fourth largest in the world, and the city has well-developed channels for Renminbi financing and trade settlement. Together with the unique advantage of its connection to the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong will help the group manage its global funds in an integrated way and make its fund operations more efficient and effective." Ms Wang added, "In the future, Chinalco Treasury will build a fully functional offshore fund management platform for the group. All funds will be pooled, all settlement will be centralised and all risks will be controlled." InvestHK has been supporting Chinalco Treasury by providing market intelligence, introducing the tax and regulatory arrangements for corporate treasury centres, and connecting it with local industry stakeholders and professional service providers. Founded in 2001, Chinalco is a key state-owned enterprise under the direct administration of the Central Government. Its industrial chain covers more than 20 non-ferrous metals, including aluminium, copper, lead and zinc, and it operates in over 20 countries and regions around the world. The group has been on the Fortune Global 500 list every year since 2008 and owns six listed companies. Under the Belt and Road Initiative, it has built a number of world-class mineral resources projects in places such as Guinea and Peru. Chinalco Treasury is wholly owned by Chinalco. For more information about Chinalco, please visit www.chinalco.com.cn .

items.title: HKSAR Government strongly condemns and firmly rejects the UK six-monthly report on Hong Kong
items.description: The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) strongly condemns and must resolutely refute the untruthful remarks, slanders and smears against various aspects of the HKSAR in the so-called six-monthly report on Hong Kong: January to June 2026 of the United Kingdom (UK) today (October 23). A spokesman for the HKSAR Government stressed, "The HKSAR is an inalienable part of the People's Republic of China, and as a local administrative region that enjoys a high degree of autonomy under the principle of 'One Country, Two Systems', comes directly under the jurisdiction of the Central People's Government. The HKSAR steadfastly safeguards national sovereignty, security and development interests, and fully and faithfully lives up to this top priority of the 'One Country, Two Systems' principle. The HKSAR Government strongly condemns and firmly rejects the UK's attempt through a so-called six-monthly report to make misleading and irresponsible remarks about Hong Kong matters, distort facts and reverse right and wrong, and attempt to interfere in the HKSAR Government's law-based governance by despicable political maneuvers." "The core essence of the Sino-British Joint Declaration is about China's resumption of the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong. It did not authorise the UK to interfere in Hong Kong's affairs after its return to the motherland. The UK has no sovereignty, jurisdiction or right of supervision over Hong Kong after its return to the motherland. The HKSAR Government strongly urges the UK again to discern facts from fallacies, respect the international law and basic norms governing international relations, and immediately stop its long-arm jurisdiction and interference in Hong Kong matters, which are purely China's internal affairs." Safeguarding Rights and Freedoms The HKSAR Government spokesman said, "The HKSAR Government steadfastly safeguards the rights and freedoms enjoyed by Hong Kong people as protected under the law. Since Hong Kong's return to the motherland, human rights in the city have always been robustly guaranteed constitutionally by both the Constitution and the Basic Law. The offences endangering national security stipulated by the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL) and the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance (SNSO) target acts endangering national security with precision, and define the elements and penalties of the offences with clarity. The relevant laws do not affect normal exchanges of local institutions, organisations and individuals with other countries, regions and international organisations including the United Nations. Law-abiding persons will not unwittingly violate the law." "The HKNSL and SNSO clearly stipulate that human rights shall be respected and protected in safeguarding national security in the HKSAR, and that the rights and freedoms, including the freedoms of speech, of the press, of publication, of association, of assembly, of procession and of demonstration that Hong Kong residents enjoy under the Basic Law and the provisions of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights as applied to Hong Kong, shall be protected in accordance with the law. Nonetheless, just as the case with other places in the world, such rights and freedoms are not absolute. The ICCPR also expressly states that some of them may be subject to restrictions as prescribed by law that are necessary for protection of national security, public safety, public order or the rights and freedoms of others, etc. The so-called report biasedly quoted figures to twist the facts by negating the determination and dedication of the HKSAR to persistently safeguard the lawful exercise of rights and freedom by citizens. The HKSAR Government must set the record straight and such act must be strongly condemned." "Since the implementation of the HKNSL and the SNSO, the media landscape in Hong Kong has remained vibrant. However, some people with ulterior motives deliberately fabricated facts about freedom of the press and speech in Hong Kong. In fact, freedom of the press and speech are firmly protected in Hong Kong at a constitutional level under the Basic Law, but they are not absolute. The media, like everyone else, have an obligation to abide by all the laws. The media continue to enjoy the freedom to comment on and criticise government policies without any restriction, as long as this is not in violation of the law. The court further cited precedents from the European Court of Human Rights regarding press freedom in the reasons for a verdict of a relevant case, pointing out that the European Convention on Human Rights does not guarantee a wholly unrestricted freedom of speech even with respect to press coverage on matters of serious public concern. The most crucial point is that journalists must act in good faith and on accurate factual basis and provide reliable and precise information in accordance with the tenets of 'responsible journalism' in order to enjoy the protection of their rights to freedom of speech and press freedom. The so-called 'World Press Freedom Index' cited in the report was published by an organisation self-claimed as 'Reporters Without Borders'. Its funding has largely come from the European Union, the United States (US) State Department and other European governments, which merely serves as a tool for anti-China forces for the US and some western countries. The so-called 'rankings' lack credibility and can be disregarded. In fact, in recent years, the police of the UK have on numerous occasions arrested journalists in the name of counter-terrorism, including the recent arrest in Leicestershire of several journalists covering pro-Palestinian activities. This further highlights that the so-called safeguard of press freedom by the UK is merely a double standard in serving political ends." Laws Safeguarding National Security The HKSAR Government spokesman said, "The HKSAR Government strongly opposes the absurd and false contents in the UK's so-called six-monthly report with regard to the laws and the relevant efforts that safeguard national security in the HKSAR. It is each and every sovereign state's inherent right, under international law and international practice based on the Charter of the United Nations, to enact laws safeguarding national security, and it is also an international practice. Western countries, including the UK, maintain extensive and strict national security legal frameworks. There are at least 14 pieces of laws safeguarding national security in the UK. In June 2026, the UK Government introduced the National Security (State Threats) Bill 2026 in order to further expand the law enforcement powers and introduce new offences. On the ground of imminency, Parliament was requested to adopt the fast-track procedure to expedite the Parliamentary progress of the Bill. As a result, the Bill had its third reading and passed by the Parliament within a month. As of June 2026, the UK authorities arrested nearly 4 000 people pursuant to national security and counter-terrorism laws; representing 15 times increase compared to the same period of time last year and more than 15 times the median in the last 10 years. Majority of such arrests were associated with demonstrators supporting an organization that was proscribed under the Terrorism Act 2000 by the UK Government. Just this past September 2026, more than 50 people were arrested simply because they held home-made banners peacefully in a protest in support of that proscribed organization, or because they were wearing or carrying an article supporting that proscribed organization, one of those arrested was a 94 years old barrister. The UK Government while swiftly and resolutely enforcing its harsh national security legislation, made large scale arrests of protesters in support of the proscribed organization under the Terrorism Act despite its decision to proscribe the relevant organization is subject to widespread criticisms. Yet, the UK Government smeared the HKNSL, which targets only a very small number of criminals endangering national security, and other relevant laws of the HKSAR, as well as the HKSAR law enforcement, prosecutorial and judicial authorities' performance of their duties in accordance with the law as 'undermining the rights and freedoms', and continued to unscrupulously distort the facts to criticize. This clearly exposes its hypocritical double standards, which are utterly ugly and despicable." "In fact, the implementation of the HKNSL in the past six years or so has enabled the livelihood and economic activities of the Hong Kong community at large to swiftly return to normal and the business environment to be restored and improved continuously. Besides maintaining its position as the world's freest economy, Hong Kong has risen to top spot in cross boundary wealth management worldwide and is ranked second in world competitiveness. The city is ranked third among international financial centres, ranked first globally in terms of funds raised through initial public offerings, and continues to set new fundraising records in 2026: total funds raised in the first three quarters exceeded HK$388 billion, more than doubling the figure for the same period last year and setting a record for the highest amount raised in the first nine months of any year to date. Hong Kong comes first in the world in terms of funds raised through initial public offerings in 2025. Hong Kong remains high and unchanged in the overall ranking and continues to be ahead of the individual Western countries which often unreasonably criticise the rule of law and human rights situation of Hong Kong in the 2026 World Justice Project Rule of Law Index. These internationally recognised achievements are built upon the freedom and stability brought to Hong Kong society by the HKNSL, other relevant laws of the HKSAR, and the work of safeguarding national security." "Hong Kong is a society underpinned by the rule of law and has always adhered to the principle that 'laws must be obeyed and lawbreakers be held accountable'. Article 5 of the HKNSL and section 2 of the SNSO clearly stipulate that the principle of the rule of law shall be adhered to in preventing, suppressing and imposing punishment for offences endangering national security. The HKSAR law enforcement agencies have been taking law enforcement actions based on evidence and strictly in accordance with the law in respect of the acts of the persons or entities concerned, which have nothing to do with their political stance, background or occupation. All cases are handled strictly on the basis of evidence and in accordance with the law. All defendants will receive fair trial strictly in accordance with laws applicable to Hong Kong (including the HKNSL) and as protected by the Basic Law and the Hong Kong Bill of Rights. Any suggestion that certain individuals or organisations should be immune from legal consequences for their illegal acts is no different from advocating a special privilege to break the law, and this totally runs contrary to the spirit of the rule of law." "As to the so-called report's malicious smears against the verdict of the case of Lai Chee-ying involving offences endangering national security (Lai's case), the HKSAR Government must stress that the court's 855-pages long reasons for verdict is reasoned and well founded, backed by solid legal grounds and rigorous analysis, and is fully open for public inspection. It fully demonstrates that the court arrived at the verdict in strict accordance with the laws and evidence, free from any interference. The court also clearly pointed out in the reasons for verdict that Lai Chee-ying was not on trial for his political views or beliefs. The reasons for sentence also provided a detailed explanation of the considerations regarding sentence factors, unequivocally identified Lai Chee-ying as the mastermind and the driving force behind the conspiracies, and the offences committed fell within the category of offences of 'a grave nature'. Lai Chee-ying opted not to appeal against his conviction or sentence. It is such a disgrace for the UK, when being faced with these ironclad facts, to continue to distort the truth and maliciously attack. The HKSAR Government must again firmly refute these claims to set the record straight." "It is important to reiterate that Lai's case has nothing to do with freedom of the press. One should not conflate criminal acts in Lai's case with freedom of the press. Lai Chee-ying repeatedly colluded with external forces to beg for sanctions and hostile activities against the Central Authorities and the HKSAR Government. It is abundantly clear that Lai Chee-ying, along with other defendants of Lai’s case, used journalism as a guise to commit acts endangering national security." "On the other hand, the HKSAR Government noticed that certain individuals with ulterior motives have fabricated lies concerning Lai's health and custodial arrangements, and it must be stressed that the Correctional Services Department (CSD) handles the custodial arrangements for Lai Chee-ying in the same way as other persons-in-custody (PICs). Regardless of the identities, ages and nationalities of the PICs, the CSD has all along been ensuring that the custodial environment for each and every PICs is safe, humane, appropriate and healthy, which includes appropriate and timely medical support. The medical services received by Lai Chee-ying in custody are adequate and comprehensive." "As to the allowing of the appeal by the Court of Appeal regarding the two counts of 'fraud' of Lai Chee-ying mentioned by the so-called report, it must be stressed that Lai Chee-ying has exploited valuable public resources of the HKSAR for over 20 years. Although the Court of Appeal considered that, in the factual context of this case, the breach in question did not reach the criminal conviction threshold for the offence of 'fraud', the objective fact remains that Lai Chee-ying has exploited public resources for private use." "In respect of the incitement to subversion case of the 'Hong Kong Alliance' mentioned by the so-called report, the verdict handed down by the court is forceful and compelling, as well as well-reasoned and sound. The reasons for verdict clearly emphasised that the defendants were put on trial not because of their political views or beliefs. The court would only consider the laws and evidence relevant to the case to decide whether the prosecution is able to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt. The court also pointed out that the defendants had all along been hostile towards the Communist Party of China and the Central Government under its leadership, and, after the implementation of the HKNSL, refused to pull back from the brink and were bent on embracing the resistance line to the very end. Even though the defendants knew that what they had said and done might have already gone beyond the scope of lawful freedom of expression, they paid no regard to it. The court reiterated in its reasons for sentence that the HKNSL had no retrospective effect and that the defendants were put on trial not because of their political ideology or their conduct before the HKNSL. They were convicted solely on the basis that they had committed acts prohibited under the HKNSL after the HKNSL came into effect. The court's reasons for sentence have clearly and in detail set out the considerations for sentencing, including reasons for determining that the case falls within the category of 'an offence of a serious nature'." "Appropriate extraterritorial effect for the offences under the HKNSL and the SNSO fully aligns with the principles of international law, international practice and common practice adopted in various countries and regions. It is both necessary and legitimate, and is also in line with those of other countries and regions around the world. As the law enforcement department of the HKSAR safeguarding national security, the Hong Kong Police are duty-bound to pursue the liability of those who have allegedly endangered national security outside Hong Kong. Those absconders hiding outside Hong Kong are wanted because they continue to blatantly engage in activities endangering national security. Moreover, they continue to collude with external forces to cover for their evil deeds. It is necessary for the Police to take all lawful measures to strongly combat the acts of abscondment, and such actions are fully justified, necessary and legitimate. Quite a number of countries including the UK would also impose measures on wanted criminals to combat the acts of abscondment. It is indeed a demonstration of hypocrisy with double standards by the UK with ulterior motives that, after the HKSAR Government has announced the relevant measures, attack the HKSAR in safeguarding national security dutifully, faithfully and in accordance with the law." "As to the case regarding the father of an absconder named Anna Kwok Fung-yee being convicted of 'attempting to deal with, directly or indirectly, any funds or other financial assets or economic resources belonging to, or owned or controlled by, a relevant absconder' as mentioned in the so-called report, as stressed in the Reasons for Sentence, the purpose of the relevant offence is to prevent anyone from dealing with the assets of an absconder, thereby increasing the chance of such absconder refusing to return to Hong Kong. The nature of the case was also considered serious, and it was reiterated that no 'collective punishment' is involved in the case and that the sentence has nothing to do with whether the defendant is related to the absconder." "We noticed that the so-called report mentioned other cases on offences endangering national security. The HKSAR Government has emphasised time and again that as the legal proceedings involving the concerned cases are still ongoing, it is inappropriate for any person to comment on the details of the case in an attempt to interfere with the court to exercise judicial power independently, which might otherwise constitute perverting the course of justice. The UK must stop distorting the truth, blatantly discrediting the judicial system and trials of the HKSAR, in an attempt to glorify criminal behavior and exert pressure on the courts of the HKSAR." "The HKSAR Government made amendments to the Implementation Rules for Article 43 of the Law of the People’s Republic of China on Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (the Amendment Rules) to enhance measures that the law enforcement authorities of the HKSAR may take and further clarify relevant legal procedures and technical arrangements, so as to strengthen the enforcement power of law enforcement authorities, prevent and investigate cases concerning offences endangering national security more effectively, and prevent and mitigate risks to national security in a timely manner. The making of the Amendment Rules is in conformity with the Basic Law, including the provisions concerning human rights, as well as the relevant provisions under the Hong Kong National Security Law. The Amendment Rules set out stringent requirements by providing in detail under what circumstances the law enforcement authorities can exercise the powers; and incorporating mechanisms with the Judiciary playing the gatekeeping role for various measures introduced by the Amendment Rules, with a view to ensuring that when law enforcement officers carry out various measures, acts and activities endangering national security can be effectively prevented, suppressed and punished, and at the same time the lawful rights and interests of individuals and organizations are adequately protected in accordance with the requirements of Article 4 and Article 5 of the Hong Kong National Security Law." Safeguarding Due Administration of Justice and Rule of Law The HKSAR Government spokesman pointed out, "The HKSAR Government safeguards independent judicial power and fully supports the Judiciary in exercising its judicial power independently, safeguarding the due administration of justice and the rule of law. Articles 2, 19 and 85 of the Basic Law specifically provide that the HKSAR enjoys independent judicial power, including that of final adjudication, and the courts of the HKSAR shall exercise judicial power independently, free from any interference. When adjudicating cases concerning offence endangering national security, as in any other cases, judges remain independent and impartial in performing their judicial duties, free from any interference. The implementation of the HKNSL over the past six years or so has proven that the courts have handled all the cases involving the HKNSL and other laws safeguarding national security in the HKSAR strictly in accordance with the above principles." "The Department of Justice takes charge of criminal prosecutions, free from any interference by virtue of Article 63 of the Basic Law. All prosecutorial decisions are based on an objective analysis of all admissible evidence and applicable laws. In addition, Article 5 of the HKNSL and section 2 of the SNSO clearly stipulate that the principle of the rule of law shall be adhered to in preventing, suppressing and imposing punishment for offences endangering national security." "The Judiciary exercises judicial power independently in accordance with the law, and everyone charged with a criminal offence has the right to a fair hearing. The courts decide cases strictly in accordance with the evidence and all applicable laws. Cases will never be handled any differently owing to the profession, political beliefs or background of the persons involved. The prosecution has the burden to prove beyond reasonable doubt the commission of an offence before a defendant may be convicted by the court." "The making of the Safeguarding National Security (Procedural Matters) Regulation (Procedural Matters Regulation) under section 110 of the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance by the HKSAR Government is only to state clearly the classification mechanism under the HKNSL and the SNSO for 'other offences endangering national security under the law of the HKSAR', in order to bring more certainty for relevant provisions of the HKNSL and the SNSO. Neither does the relevant regulation have any retrospective effect, nor creates any new offence or altering the penalty of any offence." "Regarding the mechanism concerning the certificate to be issued by the Chief Executive under Article 47 of the HKNSL or section 115 of the SNSO, owing to the inherent nature of matters concerning national security, the executive authority is in a far better position than the courts to make appropriate judgements. Hence, the courts will afford deference to the judgements made by the executive authority regarding national security matters. This principle is also a general rule for safeguarding national security practised by different places in the world, including in the UK. In a judgment by the House of Lords in 2003, the Court states that 'Under the constitution of the United Kingdom and most other countries, decisions as to whether something is or is not in the interests of national security are not a matter for judicial decision. They are entrusted to the executive.' The so-called report, however, pays no regard to the fact that the mechanism of the issuing of certificate by the Chief Executive is entirely consistent with common law principles, which we deplore." Improved Electoral System A spokesman for the HKSAR Government said, "The Legislative Council (LegCo) formed following the improvement of the electoral system in 2021 has fully implemented the principle of 'patriots administering Hong Kong', which is consistent with the universally prevailing political tenet of keeping political power in the hands of patriots. The LegCo has completely broken free from the past chaos of confrontation, polarisation, disorderly conduct and ineffectiveness in the chamber, returning to the right track of rationality and pragmatism. It deliberated with efficiency and quality, focusing its efforts on developing the economy and improving people's livelihood, ensuring the steady and successful implementation of ‘One Country, Two Systems’. The general election for the eighth term LegCo was successfully held at the end of last year. Voters actively cast their votes, returning a new cohort of LegCo members who are patriotic and love Hong Kong, responsible, capable and committed to serving the community. This has once again exemplified the high-quality and healthy competition under the new electoral system, embodying broad representation and balanced participation. The improved LegCo has proven in practice that this is a democratic electoral system that suits HKSAR's actual circumstances and needs." The spokesman continued: "As stated in the white paper Hong Kong: Democratic Progress Under the Framework of One Country, Two Systems published by the Central Government, Britain exercised a typical colonial rule over Hong Kong in the past. It did not bring any genuine democracy to Hong Kong; instead, it laid hidden snares for the development of democracy in Hong Kong after its return to China. The British side should recognise the facts and positively view Hong Kong’s democratic development as returning to the right track, as well as the achievements we have made in practising and improving a healthy democratic politics that suits Hong Kong’s actual circumstances and is effective and viable." Enhancing National Education The HKSAR Government spokesman pointed out, "Schools are places for students to learn and grow. It is the obligation of schools to provide a safe and orderly school environment and atmosphere, and to maintain a campus free from political interference or illegal activities, for safeguarding students' well-being. National education has been an important part of the curriculum for primary and secondary schools as well as kindergartens, for deepening our students' understanding of the country's development, the history and culture, the Constitution and the Basic Law, as well as national security, thereby building up cultural confidence to foster a sense of national identity, and cultivating them into an able and virtuous new generation with a sense of responsibility, visions and love for the country and the city. Teachers are also important role models of their students, playing a vital role in passing on knowledge and nurturing students' character. The HKSAR Government has the responsibility to ensure the professional conduct of teachers. Implementation of national education, including national security education, is the legitimate duty of education authorities all over the world. Different places attach great importance to implementing national security education and developing their students' sense of national identity, including knowledge of their respective constitution, their own history, culture, geography, etc." "Academic freedom is an important social value treasured in Hong Kong and the cornerstone of our higher education sector. Since the implementation of the HKNSL, academics or post-secondary education institutions in Hong Kong continue to conduct normal exchange activities with their foreign or external counterparts. Meanwhile, post-secondary institutions in Hong Kong have taken a series of measures to incorporate national security education into students' learning in fulfilment of their statutory duty. These institutions enjoy autonomy on curriculum design, and the HKSAR Government encourages the institutions to provide students with diversified learning opportunities on national security education."

items.title: SCST congratulates Hong Kong, China athletes on winning nine more medals today in Asian Para Games
items.description: The Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism, Miss Rosanna Law, today (October 22) extended her congratulations to swimming athlete Chan Yui-lam on winning a gold medal in Women's 100m Butterfly S14 at the 5th Asian Para Games, bringing the Hong Kong, China delegation its second gold medal of the Games. Miss Law also congratulated fencing athletes Fan Pui-shan, Lam Ka-man, Tong Nga-ting and Yu Chui-yee on winning a silver medal in Women's Epee Team; table tennis athletes Lam Yan-yu and Wong Hon-lam on winning a silver medal in Mixed doubles - Class XD20; swimming athlete Lau Chiu-yee on winning a bronze medal in Women's 100m Butterfly S14; swimming athletes Cheung Tsun-lok, Wong Hon-yin, Chan Yui-lam and Lau Chiu-yee on winning a bronze medal in Mixed 4x100m Freestyle S14; table tennis athletes Tong Chi-ming and Wong Yue-ching on winning a bronze medal in Mixed doubles - Class XD14; table tennis athletes Yuen King-shing, Wong Ting-ting, Wan Wai-lok and Wong Pui-kei on winning two bronze medals in Mixed doubles - Class XD22 respectively; and badminton athlete Chu Man-kai on winning a bronze medal in Men's Singles SH6. Miss Law said, "The Hong Kong, China delegation secured nine more medals today. Competing in the butterfly stroke event today, Chan Yui-lam successfully defended her title and won the gold medal at the Asian Para Games for the third consecutive time, demonstrating her top-tier strength. Her teammate, Lau Chiu-yee, maintained a steady performance to win the bronze medal in the same event and they stood side by side on the podium. The two female athletes later teamed up with Cheung Tsun-lok and Wong Hon-yin to sprint all out in the mixed relay, joining forces to win the bronze medal. Fan Pui-shan, Lam Ka-man, Tong Nga-ting and Yu Chui-yee gave their all and fought to the very end, adding a silver medal to the fencing team. The table tennis team delivered stellar performances in the mixed doubles events; Lam Yan-yu, Wong Hon-lam, Tong Chi-ming, Wong Yue-ching, Yuen King-shing, Wong Ting-ting, Wan Wai-lok and Wong Pui-kei demonstrated superb skills and tenacity, capturing one silver and three bronze medals, a total of four medals, in a single day. Chu Man-kai fought hard against his opponent to secure the bronze medal for the badminton team. With the Hong Kong, China delegation continuing to deliver encouraging news of success, we look forward to our athletes keeping up the momentum and achieving good results." The Hong Kong, China Delegation has so far won 30 medals, namely two gold, 10 silver and 18 bronze medals, at the Asian Para Games. items.title: Digital Policy Office attaches great importance to latest cybersecurity vulnerability and appeals to all sectors to take early action and apply patches
items.description: The Digital Policy Office (DPO) said today (October 22) that it attached great importance to the critical security vulnerabilities in PHP, a web programming language widely used in backend operations of global websites. The DPO has issued Security Alert to all Government Bureaux and Departments (B/Ds) and public organisations, requesting them to conduct a comprehensive review immediately to check whether their information systems had been affected and complete all patching work as soon as possible; otherwise, the relevant systems should be temporarily taken offline or isolated to reduce the risk of malicious intrusion. Meanwhile, the DPO has completed the required patching for the web content hosting service that hosts the homepages of all B/Ds. As of now, the DPO has not received any reports of related cybersecurity incidents. In addition, the DPO appeals to the public and organisations to immediately apply patches to all affected systems. The Hong Kong Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre (HKCERT) has issued a Security Bulletin and a media message to the public today. If assistance is needed, guidance can be obtained from HKCERT via email ( hkcert@hkcert.org ), telephone (8105 6060) or online form .

items.title: LegCo Panel on Environmental Affairs visits Black Point Power Station of CLP (with photos)
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Legislative Council Secretariat: The Legislative Council Panel on Environmental Affairs visited Black Point Power Station of CLP Power Hong Kong Limited (CLP) in Tuen Mun today (October 22) to gain a deeper understanding of the power company's progress in advancing innovation and application of low-carbon energy technologies. Members first received a briefing by CLP management on its decarbonisation progress under the "Climate Vision 2050" blueprint. They noted that the power company was undertaking a trial on using hydrogen-blended natural gas for electricity generation to support Hong Kong to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050. The first phase of the project will be carried out on one of the gas-fired generation units at the power station, with approximately five per cent hydrogen to be blended with natural gas for electricity generation. The testing is expected to be completed in 2028. Members also exchanged views with representatives of CLP on areas such as importation of zero-carbon energy and related electricity facilities. Members then visited the Black Point Power Station Gallery to learn about CLP's power generation business as well as measures to enhance energy security. Members noted that the company adopts a diversified fuel mix strategy, with natural gas and nuclear accounting for about half and 30 per cent of its fuel mix respectively. It also upgrades and enhances its existing generation units continuously to improve generation efficiency and environmental performance. Afterwards, Members toured the power station's facilities on a CLP electric double-decker bus. They also learnt about the application of welding robots at the power station and how to enhance the safety and efficiency of welding work through automated procedures. Members also received a briefing on the D1 gas-fired generation unit that was put into operation in 2020. Together with the D2 unit commissioned in 2024, the proportion of CLP's gas-fired generation has increased from less than 30 per cent previously to over 50 per cent. A total of 12 members and non-members of the Panel participated in the visit.

items.title: HKETO Jakarta showcases Hong Kong cinema at Jakarta Film Week (with photos)
items.description: ​With the support of the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Jakarta (HKETO Jakarta), the Cultural and Creative Industries Development Agency (CCIDA) and the Film Development Fund, the "Hong Kong Film Gala Presentation - Jakarta" opened today (October 22) at Jakarta Film Week, featuring screenings of five acclaimed Hong Kong films and a thematic film exhibition entitled "A Tale of Two Cities: Hong Kong x Jakarta". Organised by the Asian Film Awards Academy (AFAA), "Hong Kong Film Gala Presentation - Jakarta" features three films starring legendary martial arts icon Sammo Hung, namely "Eastern Condors", "Encounter of the Spooky Kind" and "The Bodyguard", alongside two recent Hong Kong productions, "The Dating Menu" and "Dead End". The programme offers Indonesian audiences an opportunity to revisit the timeless appeal of Hong Kong action cinema classics on the silver screen while experiencing fresh perspectives of the new generation of filmmakers. Hung; lead actress of "Eastern Condors" Joyce Godenzi; and lead actress of "The Dating Menu" Rachel Leung, have travelled to Jakarta to attend the gala. HKETO Jakarta co-organised a Hong Kong Night reception last night (October 21) to promote Hong Kong cinema and encourage exchanges among film, television and cultural industry professionals attending Jakarta Film Week. Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the HKETO Jakarta, Miss Libera Cheng, said that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government is dedicated to boosting film productions and nurturing talent across different sectors of the film industry through various funding schemes. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address stated that CCIDA will continue to support Hong Kong films, as well as facilitate overseas crews filming in Hong Kong. These initiatives align with the vision set out in the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the HKSAR (2026-2030), with the aim of fostering the thriving and sustainable development of the Hong Kong film industry. Some 100 guests attended the reception, including Leung; the Executive Director of the AFAA, Ms Josie Lin; Festival Director of Jakarta Film Week, Ms Rina Damayanti; and representatives from the cultural and creative industries across the Association of Southeast Asian Nations countries. In addition to the film screenings, Hung hosted a masterclass today. He shared his martial arts training experiences and reflected on his journey in bringing Hong Kong action cinema to international prominence with Indonesian film practitioners and audiences. The thematic exhibition "A Tale of Two Cities: Hong Kong x Jakarta" is being held at FX Sudirman in Jakarta from today until October 31. Through films and related exhibits, it explores the intersections between the two cities' film and cultural scenes. Admission is free. For details about the Hong Kong Film Gala Presentation, please visit www.afa-academy.com/hkfilmgala_en/ .

items.title: CFS finds malachite green in bluefin tuna sample
items.description: The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department today (October 22) announced that malachite green was detected in a sample of bluefin tuna. The CFS is following up on the incident. A spokesman for the CFS said, "The CFS collected the above-mentioned bluefin tuna sample at the import level for testing under its routine Food Surveillance Programme. The test result showed that the sample contained malachite green at a level of 1.74 parts per billion." The spokesman said that the CFS has informed the importer concerned of the irregularity and is also tracing the source and distribution of the product concerned. Malachite green is a type of industrial dye and has been used for treating infections in fish. Currently, malachite green has been prohibited for use in food-producing animals in many countries. According to the Harmful Substances in Food Regulations (Cap. 132AF), no food sold in Hong Kong is allowed to contain malachite green. Offenders will be prosecuted and liable to a fine of $50,000 and to imprisonment for six months upon conviction. The CFS will continue to follow up on the incident and take appropriate action. An investigation is ongoing.

items.title: 2026 Maker in China SME Innovation and Entrepreneurship Global Contest - Hong Kong Chapter successfully held (with photos)
items.description: The 2026 Maker in China SME Innovation and Entrepreneurship Global Contest - Hong Kong Chapter (MiCHK) Final was held successfully at Cyberport today (October 22). "Industrialization of Flexible, Ultrathin Diamond Wafers" by DiamNEX Limited won the Champion prize, while "NeuroHarbor-AI diagnosis and treatment platform for brain diseases" by NeuroHarbor Limited and "Embodied AI Neurorehabilitation Platform" by Sharpsight Limited won the First Runner-up and Second Runner-up prizes respectively. The three winning teams will represent the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) to compete in the Global Final Contest of the Maker in China to be held in Guangzhou at the end of this year. Addressing the event, the Acting Commissioner for Digital Policy, Mr Daniel Cheung, said that the MiCHK serves as an important platform for local start-ups and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to showcase their innovation and technology (I&T) achievements and expand into the Mainland markets. It enables investors and enterprises from the Mainland to gain an understanding of Hong Kong's quality I&T outcomes, helping these enterprises tap into the Mainland market. He noted that in recent years, multiple shortlisted teams have successfully connected with enterprises. Among them, some teams have entered into co-operation agreements with Mainland governments, while others have attracted attention from investment funds. This has helped accelerate the commercialisation of technological outcomes, enhance brand influence, and further expand into both Mainland and overseas markets. Mr Cheung congratulated all award-winning teams and encouraged all participating teams to leverage the various government start-up support schemes. He also urged them to focus on the Mainland market as a key development direction, seize the opportunities presented by the nation's development of new quality productive forces, and better integrate into and serve the country's overall development. This year's competition attracted a total of 170 local innovation projects, setting an all-time high for entries. Following a preliminary screening and a semi-final held earlier, the top 10 projects advanced to the Final today. The shortlisted project teams delivered live pitches to a panel of judges from various I&T fields, competing for the Champion, First Runner-up, and Second Runner-up honours. The organiser also arranged one-on-one meetings between the 10 shortlisted project teams and investors and corporate representatives from the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, facilitating matchmaking discussions on financing and project co-operation. In addition, the shortlisted teams will have the opportunity to participate in start-up incubation programmes and exhibition events, connect with Mainland investors, establish a presence in the Mainland start-up parks, and receive professional guidance to support the commercialisation of their project outcomes and market expansion. Please refer to makerinchina.hk/ for details about the entries. With the support of the Guangzhou Municipal Industry and Information Technology Bureau, the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the People's Government of Guangzhou Municipality and the Guangzhou Municipal Huangpu District Industry and Information Technology Bureau, this is the eighth time the regional chapter has taken place in Hong Kong. The 2026 MiCHK is organised by the Digital Policy Office of the HKSAR Government, together with the China Centre for Promotion of SME Development of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of the People's Republic of China, and the China International Cooperation Association of SMEs. It is formulated by the Hong Kong Cyberport Management Company Limited and the Angel Investment Foundation.

items.title: HKICL alerts public of fraudulent websites
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority: Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited (HKICL) has recently noted two types of fraudulent websites purported to be from HKICL: Type 1: systemfps.sbs hksystemfps.sbs These fraudulent websites imitate as "Buyer Online Protection" to provide services including 1) refund to buyer, 2) unauthorised online transaction reporting, and 3) online transaction support, for online transaction over FPS payment. They intend to trick users into giving away personal document number and ID photo together with phone number for real name verification in order to get cash reward. In addition, they also trick users into providing bank name, bank account number and bank account holder's name to top up and withdraw money from their platforms' virtual wallet. Further, they direct users to a fraudster impersonating as customer service personnel. Type 2: fps-hkpay.net This fraudulent website intends to trick users into giving away login credentials. Please be reminded that Type 1 and Type 2 fraudulent websites may have multiple combinations at the end of the link, e.g.: systemfps.sbs/page/place_an_order/?uuid=refund hksystemfps.sbs/page/place_an_order/?uuid=refund fps-hkpay.net/login HKICL advises that these fraudulent websites have no affiliation with HKICL, or any business of HKICL. HKICL will not directly provide FPS service to individual members of the public or contact individual members of the public proactively under usual circumstance. The genuine official website addresses of HKICL are www.hkicl.com.hk and fps.hkicl.com.hk . HKICL urges the public to beware of suspicious calls, websites or other communications, and to remain vigilant in protecting personal information. If members of the public receive any suspicious communication purportedly from HKICL, please call HKICL's general line at 2533 1111 to verify. Members of the public who suspect that they have become the victim of fraudulent acts should report promptly to the Police.

items.title: Hong Kong Customs detects two drug trafficking cases involving incoming passengers at airport (with photos)
items.description: ​Hong Kong Customs today (October 22) detected two drug trafficking cases involving incoming air passengers at Hong Kong International Airport, and seized a total of about 8 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds with a total estimated market value of about $1.7 million. Two men were arrested. In the first case, a 30-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Bangkok, Thailand, today. During customs clearance, Customs officers found about 5kg of suspected cannabis buds inside his carry-on suitcase. He was subsequently arrested. In the second case, a 36-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Bangkok, Thailand, today. During customs clearance, Customs officers found about 3kg of suspected cannabis buds inside his carry-on suitcase. He was subsequently arrested. Investigations of both cases are ongoing. Customs will continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking activities through intelligence analysis. The department also reminds members of the public to stay alert and not to participate in drug trafficking activities for monetary return. They must not accept hiring or delegation from another party to carry controlled items into and out of Hong Kong. They are also reminded not to carry unknown items for other people. Customs will continue to apply a risk assessment approach and focus on selecting passengers from high-risk regions for clearance to combat transnational drug trafficking activities. Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment. Members of the public may report any suspected drug trafficking activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form (​ eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: OASES announces new batch of 18 strategic enterprises (with photos)
items.description: The Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises (OASES) held a signing ceremony today (October 22) to welcome a new batch of 18 strategic enterprises (see Annex) establishing or expanding their operations in Hong Kong. The ceremony was officiated by the Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan. The new cohort demonstrates the growing momentum of Hong Kong's innovation and technology (I&T) ecosystem and enterprises' confidence in the city's development prospects. Half of the new partners come from the Chinese Mainland, while the other half are from other parts of the world, underscoring Hong Kong's role as a place where businesses, talent and ideas from around the world come together to prosper. Several of the enterprises have market capitalisations or valuations exceeding HK$100 billion. The enterprises span a wide range of sectors, including advanced manufacturing, new energy, AI, life and health technology, fintech, and cultural and creative technology. They include a trailblazer in embodied AI robotics, a multinational healthcare innovator with a strong presence across pharmaceuticals and medical technologies, one of the world's largest gold refineries of precious metals service providers, a leader of next-generation financial infrastructure and digital asset solutions, and a global microelectronics leader in intelligent power management solutions, alongside pioneers in AI, physical AI, digital twins, clinical decision support, microelectronics, new energy technologies and systems, smart vehicles, new and integrated media and entertainment. With the addition of this new batch, the total number of OASES enterprises has reached 142. Together, they are expected to bring in some HK$84 billion worth of investment and create some 26 700 jobs, including high-value positions in research and development (R&D) and management over the coming years. Welcoming the new enterprises, Mr Chan said the first six batches had exceeded investment expectations by 30 per cent and job creation expectations by 34 per cent, taking up more than 2.8 million square feet of commercial and industrial space. He emphasised their role in driving I&T forward, providing new impetus to the economy and employment, and delivering solutions that make people live better. Mr Chan said I&T is a priority under Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the "four centres and one hub" framework. The Government will connect finance, research, talent and industry, with "Finance+" helping enterprises secure capital to innovate, commercialise and expand. He added that the Northern Metropolis's three planned university towns will bring education, research, talent development and industry closer together, accelerating the journey from laboratory discoveries to market-ready solutions. And through the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone, Hong Kong is making it easier for people, goods, capital, data and samples to flow across the boundary. Closer Mainland-Hong Kong collaboration on clinical trials and drug approvals will help bring new treatments to patients more quickly. Highlighting Hong Kong's openness, international connectivity and free flow of goods, capital, information and talent, Mr Chan invited enterprises to build their businesses, conduct research and nurture talent in the city, using it as a springboard to take their innovations further. The Director-General of OASES, Mr Peter Yan, said that the new cohort will further strengthen Hong Kong's strategic industries and enrich its I&T ecosystem. With initial projects spanning sectors such as fintech, clinical research, precious metals services, advanced manufacturing and embodied robotics commercialisation, the enterprises are expected to bring cutting-edge technologies, high-calibre talent and significant investment to Hong Kong. These leading enterprises will not only bring capital, technology, and talent, but also serve as "chain leaders" to cluster upstream and downstream enterprises and partners in Hong Kong. This will foster deep integration across the industry, innovation, and capital chains, further consolidating Hong Kong's position as an I&T hub. He added that OASES will continue to align its work with the National 15th Five-Year Plan and Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, while fostering a more conducive environment for attracting high-quality strategic enterprises and further consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading international I&T centre.
